posts.title: Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725) (C0017)

The physical and economic exhaustion of the region through the transformation of the Cossack host into unpaid labor for imperial construction projects. The chief of these was the Ladoga Canal: Peter I handed the direction of the works to Münnich, while the digging itself "was carried out chiefly by the hands of Ukrainian Cossacks," and "on the construction works, tens of thousands of people perished from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"[1]. In 1721 the acting hetman P. Polubotok "headed a 10,000-strong Cossack corps dispatched by order of Tsar Peter I to the construction of the Ladoga Canal"[2]. For the defiant there were also the Neva construction sites - as hard labor: captured Zaporozhians were "exiled to Sankt-Piterburkh to hard labor forever"[3].

---

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0057 Labor Exploitation January 1704 C0017 Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army (T0057Labor Exploitation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The mass mobilization of Cossack regiments for penal construction labor: the digging of the Ladoga Canal "was carried out chiefly by the hands of Ukrainian Cossacks," and there "tens of thousands of people perished from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"[1]. In 1721 a "10,000-strong Cossack corps" headed by P. Polubotok was dispatched to the canal[2]; the works continued through 1721–23[4]. |
| **[T0102 Resource Exploitation January 1704 C0017 Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government (T0102Resource Exploitation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/364):** Shifting the upkeep of the mobilized onto the subjects themselves: Cossacks dispatched to the imperial construction sites were left without supply and "suffer great want from hunger, having neither food for themselves, nor winter quarters, nor fodder for the horses"[3]. Workers for state construction the tsar simply ordered to be "taken from Ukraine, from those towns that are under your authority"[3], while at the works themselves people perished "from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"[1]. |
| **[T0036 Installation of a New System of Governance January 1704 C0017 Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army (T0036Installation of a New System of Governance)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** Removing Cossack regiments from the Cossack hierarchy and placing them under the direct command of imperial officials: Peter I handed the direction of the Ladoga Canal works to B.-C. Münnich, who "took over from Prince A. Menshikov the direction of the construction (digging) of the Ladoga Canal"[1]; Cossack corps were dispatched to these works "by order of Tsar Peter I"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Case of Pavlo Polubotok (1723)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Case of Pavlo Polubotok (1723) (C0018)

Peter I's establishment of the First Little Russian Collegium to seize governance from the hetman's administration: the collegium was created "as the highest appellate instance and the administrative-controlling organ of the Russian state structure in Ukraine"[1]. It was accompanied by the arrest of acting hetman Polubotok and the officers for defending the autonomy: "the officers submitted to Emperor Peter I yet another petition to close the Little Russian Collegium. After this, interrogations of Polubotok began in the Secret Chancellery, and on November 10, 1723 he was arrested and imprisoned in the Peter and Paul Fortress"[2], where the hetman died. The arrest order itself was never published as a separate act - the case was run by the Secret Chancellery; the circumstances were retrospectively set out in Empress Catherine I's manifesto of 8 February 1725: "it was ordered that the General Starshyna - Polubotok, Chernysh and Savych - be in St. Petersburg to answer for it"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0036 Installation of a New System of Governance January 1722 C0018 The Case of Pavlo Polubotok (1723) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0036Installation of a New System of Governance)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** The introduction of the collegium as a parallel organ of power to seize judicial and fiscal functions from the hetman's administration: it acted "as the highest appellate instance and administrative-controlling organ"[1], and "the Little Russian Collegium for the first time channeled Ukrainian finances into the tsar's treasury in full"[1]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition January 1722 C0018 The Case of Pavlo Polubotok (1723) G0009 Russian Empire S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The arrest of the acting hetman and officers in St. Petersburg for petitions defending autonomous rights. Peter was preparing a demonstrative reprisal: "Peter I planned to hold a show trial of Polubotok and his associates, accuse them of 'high treason,' and liquidate the Ukrainian autonomy. A special General Court was created for this purpose"[4]. Only the prisoner's death derailed the plan: the hetman "died on December 21, 1724 (O.S.) of pneumonia"[4]. |

posts.title: The Battle of Kruty and the Killing of Prisoners (January 1918)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Battle of Kruty and the Killing of Prisoners (January 1918) (C0019)

In late December 1917, as the troops of Bolshevik Russia were advancing on Kyiv, a detachment of yunkers - cadets of the 1st Kyiv Youth Military School named after Bohdan Khmelnytsky (four companies of 150 cadets each, 20 officers, 18 machine guns) - under the command of Sotnyk Averkii Honcharenko took up the defense of Bakhmach station, a railway junction on the border of the UNR and the RSFSR[1]. On January 27, 1918, reinforcements arrived from Kyiv - the first company of the student volunteer battalion under the command of Sotnyk Omelchenko, 115-130 volunteers: students of the Ukrainian National University and Kyiv University and senior-grade pupils of Ukrainian gymnasiums - teenagers, many of them 17 years old[1][2]. The Ukrainian forces took up defense near Kruty station (now the village of Pamiatne in Chernihiv oblast)[1]. On the morning of January 29 a six-thousand-strong detachment of Petrograd and Moscow Red Guards led by Yegorov attacked the positions; the fighting lasted until evening, the defenders repelled several attacks and, on the order of Sotnyk Averkii Honcharenko, withdrew to their echelon - the detachment's train waiting two kilometers away; their losses came to as many as 300 killed, wounded, and captured[1]. A platoon of the student company lost its bearings at dusk and came out at the station already held by the Red Guards; 27 prisoners were shot - among them, according to testimony in the investigation file of commander-in-chief Muravyov, "there were many gymnasium pupils of about 17"; Yegorov, commander of the First Revolutionary Army, authorized the shooting[2]. The teenage cadets managed to delay the offensive: explaining the heavy losses at Kruty and the delay in the advance on Kyiv, Muravyov claimed in his report that the Ukrainian forces had been commanded by "S. Petliura himself" - as the compilers of the collection of the Ukrainian Institute of National Memory note[3]. In February Muravyov's troops approached Kyiv from the Darnytsia side, shelled the city with heavy artillery for five days, and captured it on February 8, 1918[4]. After the UNR concluded the Peace of Brest-Litovsk with the Central Powers, German and Austro-Hungarian troops entered Ukraine, with Ukrainian units in the vanguard; the Bolsheviks abandoned Kyiv, and in early March the Council of People's Ministers returned there, followed a few days later by the Ukrainian Central Rada[5]. On March 19, 1918, by decision of the Ukrainian Central Rada, the bodies of those killed at Kruty were brought to Kyiv and ceremonially buried at the Askold's Grave cemetery[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0019 Military Intervention December 1917 C0019 The Battle of Kruty and the Killing of Prisoners (January 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0019Military Intervention)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** In January 1918 the troops of Bolshevik Russia were advancing on Kyiv. At Kruty station the Ukrainian defense barred their way. From late December 1917 the yunkers - cadets of the 1st Kyiv Youth Military School named after Bohdan Khmelnytsky, four companies of 150 cadets each with 20 officers and 18 machine guns - under the command of Sotnyk Averkii Honcharenko held Bakhmach, a railway junction on the border of the UNR and the RSFSR[1]. On January 27 the first company of the student volunteer battalion under Sotnyk Omelchenko arrived from Kyiv to join them - 115-130 volunteers: students and senior-grade gymnasium pupils, teenagers, many of them 17 years old[1][2]. Together with the company the Ukrainian command also sent out a demolition team; the volunteers dug in on both sides of the railway line between the stations of Kruty and Plisky[3]. The battle began on the morning of January 29, 1918. Historians of the Institute of History of Ukraine of the National Academy of Sciences write: it took place "during the offensive on the city of Kyiv by the troops of Bolshevik Russia", with the positions attacked by the forces of "a 6-thousand-strong Bolshevik detachment of Petrograd and Moscow Red Guards" led by Yegorov[1]. The fighting lasted until evening, the defenders repelled several attacks; historians put the defenders' losses at "up to 300 killed, wounded, captured"[1]. Toward evening Sotnyk Averkii Honcharenko ordered a withdrawal to their echelon - the detachment's train waiting two kilometers away; during the retreat part of the student company was encircled, and one platoon lost its bearings at dusk and came out at the station already held by the Red Guards - 27 captured teenagers and students were shot[1]. The defenders delayed the Red Guards' advance on Kyiv: explaining the heavy losses and the delay, Muravyov claimed in his report that the Ukrainian forces had been commanded by "S. Petliura himself" - as the compilers of the collection of the Ukrainian Institute of National Memory note[3]. |
| **[T0162.003 Killing of Prisoners and Detainees December 1917 C0019 The Battle of Kruty and the Killing of Prisoners (January 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0162.003Killing of Prisoners and Detainees)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/609):** The Red Guards shot the prisoners taken at Kruty (a station in the Chernihiv region) with the authorization of Yegorov, commander of the First Revolutionary Army. Lapidus, commissar of the 1st Moscow Red Guard detachment, who was with the prisoners at the station and the day before, together with Zombart, commander of the armored train, had talked the Red Guards out of an immediate reprisal, recounted in his testimony to the investigation in the case of commander-in-chief Muravyov: "The next day, as we were pulling out of Kruty station, the train stopped on the way at Yegorov's order; all the detainees were led out of the carriage, and 300 paces from the train they were shot with explosive bullets. I went up to the dead, then went up to Yegorov and asked why they had been shot. Yegorov, puffing on a cigarette and smiling, replied that he had given the Red Guards permission because they insisted on it"[2]. Moiseyev, a member of the committee of the First Revolutionary Army, described in his testimony who was shot: "At Kruty station about 20 haidamakas were taken prisoner, among them many gymnasium pupils of about 17. They were taken beyond the station and shot in the most shameless manner. There was an outrageous case when one youth ran away from that place, but he was chased down, brought back to the same spot wearing only his underwear and shot" - and specified: "this was done from the train commanded by Yegorov"[2]. Babenko, commander of the Moscow detachment, captured the prisoners, and Muravyov had appointed Yegorov commander of the First Army - both links are recorded in the investigation materials[2]. The investigation clarified the number of those shot: Tsvanger, secretary of the army committee, corrected her testimony, naming 24 people instead of the earlier 150, and a member of the investigative commission certified the correction[3]. The sources differ in describing the manner of the killing: Sotnyk Averkii Honcharenko, who commanded the Ukrainian detachment at Kruty, wrote in his memoirs that the prisoners were not shot but bayoneted, whereas the documents of the Soviet investigation record shooting with explosive bullets[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Moscow Articles of Ivan Briukhovetsky (1665)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Moscow Articles of Ivan Briukhovetsky (1665) (C0024)

The treaty that became the point of no return in the political, economic, and military absorption of the autonomy: "Under the Moscow Articles, direct control over the military-administrative and financial-economic life of Ukraine (except for the Cossack estate) passed into the hands of the tsarist voivodes"[1]. Garrisons headed by voivodes were introduced into new cities as far as Kodak, taxes went directly to the tsar's treasury, and the Kyiv metropolitanate was to be subordinated to the Moscow patriarch[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0041 Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel September 1665 C0024 The Moscow Articles of Ivan Briukhovetsky (1665) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army (T0041Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/345):** Expansion of the military occupation of the autonomy: in addition to reinforcing the garrisons of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Pereiaslav, and Nizhyn, "Russian military garrisons headed by voivodes were introduced into Poltava, Kremenchuk, Novhorod-Siverskyi, Oster, Kaniv, and other cities, as well as into Kodak in the Liberties of the Zaporozhian Host"[1] – the upkeep of the troops was placed on Ukrainian taxpayers. |

The collected funds were channeled into the tsar's treasury"[1]. |

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Konotop Articles of Ivan Samoilovych (1672) (C0025)

A further curtailment of the Hetmanate's political agency and interference in the autonomy's internal affairs: "Overall, the Konotop Articles limited the hetman's power in favor of the officer oligarchy, and also narrowed the autonomy of the Hetmanate"[1]. The weakening of the hetman's power laid the ground for the growing influence of the Muscovite government over the autonomy's elites.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0031 Restriction of Sovereignty June 1672 C0025 The Konotop Articles of Ivan Samoilovych (1672) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy (T0031Restriction of Sovereignty)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Interference in internal governance: "the hetman was deprived of the right to arbitrarily (without a hearing before the military court) issue orders for the execution or dismissal of his subordinates"[2] – personnel and judicial decisions were removed from the hetman's sole authority. The norm itself is older than this treaty: it was first fixed by the Konotop Articles of 1672 ("executed and removed from office… by the judgment and proof of the Host's court")[3]. |
| **[T0015 Bribery of Elites June 1672 C0025 The Konotop Articles of Ivan Samoilovych (1672) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy (T0015Bribery of Elites)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/324):** A wager on the estate interests of the officer class: "The Konotop Articles limited both the hetman's power and, accordingly, the autonomy of the Hetmanate, while significantly expanding the rights of the Cossack officers"[2] – by expanding the rights of the officer oligarchy at the hetman's expense, Moscow gained levers of influence over the autonomy through the hands of its own elite. |

</details>

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Liquidation of the Cossacks in Right-Bank Ukraine (1699) (C0026)

The destruction of the Cossack regimental order on the Right Bank by a decision of the Polish Sejm of 1699, on lands that Moscow and Warsaw had divided along the Dnipro by the "Eternal Peace" of 1686. Colonel Palii "did not accept the decisions of the general Sejm of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth of 1699 banning the Cossacks on the Right Bank" and "contrary to the terms of the 'Eternal Peace' of 1686 pursued a policy of uniting the Right Bank and the Left Bank"[1].

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Decisive Points (1728) (C0028)

A unilateral imperial act imposed on hetman Danylo Apostol instead of the traditional bilateral treaty. While formally softening the regime of the Little Russian Collegium, the document entrenched harsh imperial restrictions on key points: "Article 19 forbids the hetman relations with other countries"[1], customs revenues went to the tsar's treasury, and personnel appointments were placed under the metropole's control.

---

The autonomy ceased to be a party to a treaty and received its rules of existence from above. |

posts.title: The Governing Council of the Hetman Government and the Lubny Treaty (1734–1750)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Governing Council of the Hetman Government and the Lubny Treaty (1734–1750) (C0029)

A long period of direct rule over the Left Bank without the election of a hetman. "The GOVERNANCE OF THE HETMAN'S GOVERNMENT was an organ of power created by the government of Russian empress Anna in 1734 after the death of hetman D. Apostol to govern Left-Bank Ukraine (the Hetmanate) and to prevent new hetman elections"; "in essence its head was the tsar's resident"[1]. At the same time the empire brought Zaporizhzhia back under control: "Anna amnestied the Zaporozhians and allowed them to return to the old Sich grounds (1734) and found the New Sich"[2] – on the eve of war with Turkey the Cossacks were being brought back as a military resource of the crown.

---

posts.title: Liquidation of the Institution of the Hetmancy and the Second Little Russian Collegium (1764)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Liquidation of the Institution of the Hetmancy and the Second Little Russian Collegium (1764) (C0030)

The final abolition of political autonomy. Catherine II forced hetman Rozumovsky to renounce his office and by the decree of November 10, 1764 established an occupation administration: "we command our Senate, for the proper governance of Little Russia, to establish there a Little Russian Collegium, presided over by our general, Count Rumyantsev"[1]. The program had been set in advance in a secret instruction: "so that they become Russified and cease looking to the forest like wolves"[2].

---

|---|
| **[T0008 Deprivation of Agency November 1764 C0030 Liquidation of the Institution of the Hetmancy and the Second Little Russian Collegium (1764) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0008Deprivation of Agency)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** The final elimination of the office of the autonomy's leader: after Rozumovsky's forced abdication, Catherine II's decree of November 10, 1764 handed power to the Little Russian Collegium, whose president was instructed to act "with a governor's authority, that is, as our special plenipotentiary"[1]. Catherine II's instruction to procurator-general Vyazemsky (1764) stated the goal openly: "and when there is no hetman in Little Russia, one must strive that the very age and name of hetmans vanish"[2]. |

The diplomatic severing of Crimea from the Ottoman Empire through the recognition of a fictitious "independence": under Article III of the treaty, "All the Tatar peoples: the Crimean, Budjak, Kuban, Yedisan, Jamboyluk, and Yedichkul, without exception, are to be recognized by both empires as free and entirely independent of any outside power"[1] – this "independence" became the prologue to the annexation of the peninsula nine years later.

posts.title: Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775) (C0033)

The military encirclement and destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich immediately after a joint war. Catherine II's manifesto of 3 August 1775 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XX, no. 14,354) declared: "the Zaporozhian Sich has been utterly destroyed, with the extirpation for the future of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks"[1][2]. The last kish otaman, Kalnyshevsky, "was arrested and sent to the prison of the Solovetsky monastery"[3], where he spent more than 25 years. Hrushevsky describes the mechanics of the treachery: the government "went about the affair slowly, in secret, to catch the Zaporozhians entirely unprepared," and general Tekeli "entered the Zaporozhian lands as a good friend" - then suddenly laid siege to the Sich. The Zaporozhians were even faulted for their own husbandry: they "were establishing their own tillage and thereby severing their dependence on the Russian state"[4].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0019 Military Intervention May 1775 C0033 Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army (T0019Military Intervention)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The encirclement and forcible seizure of the Sich by imperial troops right after the Cossacks had helped the empire win the war. The manifesto records the operation matter-of-factly: "On June 4, Our Lieutenant-General Tekeli, with the troops entrusted to him by us, occupied the Zaporozhian Sich"[1]. |
| **[T0045 Destruction of Historical Memory May 1775 C0033 Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0045Destruction of Historical Memory)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/349):** The issuing of Catherine II's August manifesto, officially erasing the very memory of the Sich: it was destroyed "with the extirpation for the future of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks," for the empire resolved "to destroy the Zaporozhian Sich and the name of the Cossacks derived from it"[1]. Hrushevsky: "The Sich was destroyed, and on 3 August a tsarist decree announced its abolition, 'with the annihilation of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks'"[4]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition May 1775 C0033 Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775) G0009 Russian Empire S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The arrest and exile of the Sich's top leadership: "In July 1775, after the destruction of the New Sich, by order of Empress Catherine II, Kalnyshevsky was arrested and sent to the prison of the Solovetsky monastery"[3]. Kalnyshevsky spent more than 25 years in confinement; formally freed in 1801, he died in the monastery. |

</details>

# Campaign: Administrative Dismantling and Enserfment of the Left Bank (1781–1786) (C0034)

The execution of Catherine II's secret instructions for the institutional and cultural assimilation of the land: the liquidation of the regimental order and the introduction of imperial viceroyalties – the Kyiv Viceroyalty was established by the nominal decree to the Senate of September 16, 1781 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XXI, no. 15,228; execution ordered from November)[1][2], "which finally abolished the remnants of the Hetmanate's autonomy and its regimental-sotnia administrative-political and military order"[3]; the secularization of monastery lands in 1786 and the legal binding of peasants by Catherine II's decree of May 3, 1783: "each of the villagers is to remain in the place and station where he is registered by the current last revision"[4].

posts.title: Military Annexation of the Crimean Khanate (1783)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Military Annexation of the Crimean Khanate (1783) (C0035)

The seizure of the Crimean Khanate and its forcible incorporation into the Russian Empire: "WE have resolved to take under OUR dominion the Crimean peninsula, the island of Taman, and the entire Kuban side"[1]. With regard to Ukraine, the annexation was secured through the forced mobilization of Cossacks as a military resource, the colonization of the adjacent southern steppes to create a loyal rear, and the erasure of Cossack toponyms: the lands of the destroyed Sich were assigned by Catherine II's manifesto of 3 August 1775 "as convenient to the Novorossiysk Governorate"[2]. For Crimea this meant the liquidation of the state and its ruling dynasty: "in the spring of 1782 Khan Shahin Girey was forced to flee under Russian protection"[3], the manifesto on the taking of Crimea was signed by Catherine II on April 8, 1783 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XXI, no. 15,108)[4], and the khan was exiled to Kaluga; the indigenous population was being squeezed out in waves of emigration - "if before 1787 only 8 thousand had emigrated, by 1792 it was already tens of thousands"[3].

---

| **[T0117.001 Migratory Replacement April 1783 C0035 Military Annexation of the Crimean Khanate (1783) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0117.001Migratory Replacement)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/389):** The colonization of the steppes adjacent to Crimea with settlers to create a loyal rear: as early as 1752, New Serbia was formed from Serbs – "officially – to guard the southern frontiers from Tatar and Turkish raids, but in fact – to subdue the Zaporozhians"[7], and in 1776 Potemkin directly ordered "not to return fugitives"[8], accelerating the settlement of the south. |
| **[T0043 Erasure and Renaming of Place Names April 1783 C0035 Military Annexation of the Crimean Khanate (1783) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0043Erasure and Renaming of Place Names)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/347):** The erasure of the historical names of the Cossack southern territories used as a springboard for the annexation of Crimea: Catherine II's manifesto of 3 August 1775 extirpated "the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks" and poured their lands into an imperial construct – "assigning them as convenient to the Novorossiysk Governorate"[2]. |

The introduction of discriminatory legislation that territorially restricted the rights of the Jewish population: decree No. 17,006 of December 23, 1791 confirmed the ban on Jews enrolling in the merchantry in the internal Russian cities and ports, extending the rights of citizenship and burgher status only to the Ekaterinoslav Viceroyalty and the Tauride region[1]. posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Creation of the Little Russian Governorate-General (1801–1811) (C0038)

Administrative absorption: "the LITTLE RUSSIAN GOVERNORATE-GENERAL – an administrative-territorial and political unit of the Russian Empire, created in 1802 for the incorporation and integration of Left-Bank Ukraine into the Russian Empire"[1]. The outcome is recorded there as well: "During the existence of the governorate-general, the remnants of the Hetmanate's autonomy were finally liquidated"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0030 Administrative-Territorial Division January 1801 C0038 Creation of the Little Russian Governorate-General (1801–1811) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0030Administrative-Territorial Division)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The erasure of historical borders and the introduction of the imperial vertical: "The governor-general concentrated the entire fullness of administrative power: he was endowed with the right of legislative initiative, determined the degree to which all-Russian laws extended within the governorate-general, and controlled the activity of state institutions, including judicial ones"[1]. |
| **[T0158 Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols January 1801 C0038 Creation of the Little Russian Governorate-General (1801–1811) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0158Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** In 1804-1811 the Russian Empire put up a cast-iron Monument of Glory in the center of Poltava in memory of its victory over the army of Charles XII on 27 June 1709 - with the city's own money and to a design sent from St. Petersburg. By the imperial decree to the Senate of 11 September 1804, "On leaving the villages formerly owned by the city of Poltava under state administration and on releasing the income collected from them to the local Governor-General for the construction in Poltava of a monument in memory of 27 June 1709," the city's revenues were assigned to the monument: "the community of Poltava citizens, through a petition submitted to Governor-General Prince Kurakin, has designated all these revenues for the construction in Poltava of a monument in memory of the day unforgettable for Russia, 27 June 1709, and so we command: the revenues now due for payment, as well as those henceforth collected in favor of this city, shall be released to the local Governor-General until the monument that has been begun is completely finished"[2]. By a second act, the imperial rescript of 9 May 1805 to the Governor-General of Little Russia, "On the construction of a monument in commemoration of the victory won at Poltava by Emperor Peter the Great," the emperor sent a ready-made design and ordered construction to begin: "I forward to you herewith the plans for this monument, drawn up here, charging you... to proceed with its construction on site, except for the bronze ornaments belonging to it, which will be made separately here and delivered to their destination"[2]. That is, Poltava pays, while Petersburg decides what the sign on its land will look like - down to the bronze, which is cast there and shipped ready-made. The monument was founded on 27 June 1804, the cast-iron column was raised in May 1809 under the direction of Moskvin, an engineer of the Luhansk works, and the whole ensemble was opened on 27 June 1811, for the next anniversary of the battle[3][4]. On the medallion of the upper square of the pedestal, inside a serpent ring between two quivers, stood "June the 27th, 1709," and on the opposite side - "Finished in 1809"[3]: the date of someone else's victory was made into the date of the place itself. Both inscriptions, together with the bronze bas-reliefs, disappeared in 1901 - the pre-revolutionary survey records it tersely: "This inscription and the preceding one were destroyed in 1901, and at the same time the bronze bas-reliefs that surrounded them were taken by persons unknown"[3]; they were restored only during the capital repairs of 1953[4]. The monument still stands in Poltava: as of August 2026 it is listed as a monument of national significance under heritage protection number 160010-Н[5], the Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance recommended dismantling it in a letter of 29 July 2024[6], but decisions on monuments of national significance are made by the government, and the list of such decisions as of 20 May 2026 does not include the monument[7]. |

</details>

posts.title: Introduction of Military Settlements and Liquidation of the Danubian Sich (1817–1828)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Introduction of Military Settlements and Liquidation of the Danubian Sich (1817–1828) (C0041)

A campaign to turn the free population into rightless military settlers. "The trigger was the order abolishing the Buh Cossack Host and turning the Cossacks into military settlers"[1] – the Buh Cossacks' uprising of 1817 was brutally suppressed. There were two acts, on opposite sides of the uprising: the nominal decree of April 17, 1817 transferred the Buh Host's district "into direct military administration" (PSZRI, vol. XXXIV, no. 26,802) - this was the trigger; the decree of October 8, 1817 (no. 27,081), issued after the suppression, formalized the liquidation: "the name of the Buh Cossack Host is abolished"[2]. Later, kish otaman Hladky with part of the Danubian Cossacks "on May 30 (18), 1828 crossed the Kiliya mouth of the Danube, entered the port of Izmail, and joined the Russian army"[3] – this was the end of the last free host: the Danubian Sich "existed from the last quarter of the 18th century until 1828"[3].

---

# Campaign: Destruction of the Archives of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra (1718) (C0042)

A covert operation (sabotage) by Muscovite emissaries disguised as monks, aimed at the physical destruction of historical archives. The enormous archive and library burned down; the charters and grants… of princes, magnates, and hetmans perished"; historian Hyrych sums up: "The fire destroyed the written memory of the Lavra's independent Ukrainian political and spiritual life"[1].

# Campaign: Ban on Ukrainian Book Printing (1720) (C0043)

A campaign to introduce censorship and institutional linguistic assimilation. Peter I's decree of October 5, 1720 banned the printing of books in the indigenous people's language at the key printing houses: "In the Kyiv-Pechersk and Chernihiv printing houses no new books whatsoever are to be printed except previous church editions, and even those old church books are to be corrected before printing for complete conformity with the Great Russian church books, so that there be no discord or distinct dialect in them"[1].

posts.title: Russification of Education and Religion (1769–1786)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Russification of Education and Religion (1769–1786) (C0044)

A systematic campaign of the Russian Empire to root out the indigenous people's language from education and religion: "in 1769 the Holy Synod not only refused permission to print South Russian primers, but ordered the confiscation of those already in people's hands"[1]; by an order of 26 October 1784, the Kyiv metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky directed the rector and prefect of the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy "to take unremitting care of the unfailing and unomitted observance, by teachers and students alike, of the rules of Russian orthography," under the threat of expelling students from the clerical estate[2]; in 1786 the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy was prescribed the empire-wide mode of instruction[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0113.001 Legislative Ban on the Native Language January 1769 C0044 Russification of Education and Religion (1769–1786) G0009 Russian Empire S0011 Moscow Patriarchate (T0113.001Legislative Ban on the Native Language)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** The mass confiscation of national educational and religious literature: "in 1769 the Holy Synod not only refused permission to print South Russian primers, but ordered the confiscation of those already in people's hands, since the primers of that time were regarded as church books"[1]. |
| **[T0114.003 Conversion of Schools to the Metropole's Language January 1769 C0044 Russification of Education and Religion (1769–1786) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0114.003Conversion of Schools to the Metropole's Language)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/379):** The Russification of teaching in the country's principal institution of learning: from 1784 metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky introduced new classes of geography and history at the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy with an order to conduct them "in pure Russian," and by his order of 26 October 1784 demanded that teachers and students observe "the rules of orthography proper to the Russian language" - teachers faced dismissal for lapses, and students expulsion from the clerical estate[2]. The unification was completed by the order of February 13, 1786: "to adopt immediately for the Kyiv Academy the mode of instruction legalized for all schools in the All-Russian Empire"[3] – the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy was transferred to the empire-wide mode of teaching. |
| **[T0116.003 Ban on Worship in the Native Language January 1769 C0044 Russification of Education and Religion (1769–1786) G0009 Russian Empire S0011 Moscow Patriarchate (T0116.003Ban on Worship in the Native Language)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/387):** The displacement of the local population's language from the sacred sphere: metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky's order of 26 October 1784 demanded that students and future priests practice "the reading of church books of every kind, and above all the Bible, acquiring a good and pure pronunciation" - after the Moscow model instead of the Ukrainian church tradition, under the threat of expulsion from the clerical estate[2], and in 1786 metropolitan Myslavsky prescribed to the clergy the unification of pronunciation and orthography along the Russian model[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Valuev Circular: Ban on the Language and Schools (1862–1869)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Valuev Circular: Ban on the Language and Schools (1862–1869) (C0046)

A state campaign to destroy the Ukrainian language and culture: in 1862 the authorities closed the Sunday schools that taught in Ukrainian - "for the alleged presence of revolutionary propaganda"[1], the ban on the national press, the official denial of the language's existence – the Valuev circular: "there was not, is not, and cannot be any distinct Little Russian language"[2] – and bonuses to officials "in the ten South-Western governorates for persons of Russian origin, excluding, however, local natives," fixed by the decrees of 1869 and 1886[3].

---

| **[T0130 Financial Incentives for Assimilators January 1862 C0046 The Valuev Circular: Ban on the Language and Schools (1862–1869) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0130Financial Incentives for Assimilators)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/402):** The introduction of bonuses for the policy of denationalization: by decrees of the tsarist administration of 1869 and 1886, officials "in the ten South-Western governorates - persons of Russian origin, excluding, however, local natives" - were assigned bonuses for successes in the Russification of Ukraine[3] - part of the authorities' systematic plans to strengthen the "Russian assimilatory potential" of the Western krai after the Polish uprising of 1863, which included material benefits for Russian officials and teachers[4]. |

posts.title: The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887) (C0047)

The complete displacement of the language from the cultural and literary sphere. The Ems ukase prescribed: "Not to permit the import into the empire… of any books whatsoever published abroad in the Little Russian dialect," "To forbid in the empire the printing, in the same dialect, of any original works or translations whatsoever," and "To forbid likewise any stage performances, texts to musical scores, and public readings in the same dialect"[1]. The permitted dictionaries were allowed only "on condition of their being printed in conformity with all-Russian orthography"[2].

Five years later the rules were revised by a Special Conference - it included Solsky, Ostrovsky, the chief procurator of the Synod Pobedonostsev, and Viazemsky, - and the minister of internal affairs Ignatiev reported the result to the emperor on 3 October 1881; assent followed on 8 October[3]. There were no plans to publish the revision, and Ignatiev explained why: "the rules on the use of the Little Russian dialect established in 1876 were not promulgated, and therefore it is not intended to make the projected clarifications known to the general public"[3]. The circular went out to governor-general Drenteln on 16 October stamped "Confidential"[3] - that is, people were judged by rules they were never shown.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (5)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0113.001 Legislative Ban on the Native Language January 1876 C0047 The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0113.001Legislative Ban on the Native Language)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** A total legislative ban on the language: "Not to permit the import into the empire… of any books whatsoever published abroad in the Little Russian dialect"; "To forbid likewise any stage performances, texts to musical scores, and public readings in the same dialect"[1]. |
| **[T0115.001 Replacement of the Native Language's Alphabet January 1876 C0047 The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0115.001Replacement of the Native Language's Alphabet)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/381):** A concession that was in fact a choice between two alien orthographies: the 1881 revision allowed dictionaries to be printed, but "on condition of their being printed in conformity with all-Russian orthography, or with the orthography used in Little Russia no later than the 18th century"[3]. That is, either the metropole's orthography or an archaic one was admissible - contemporary Ukrainian orthography was not allowed in any form. The same document permitted stage texts to musical scores to be printed only "on condition of generally accepted Russian orthography," and made Ukrainian-language performances dependent on administrative permission: "dramatic plays, scenes and couplets in the Little Russian dialect... may be performed on stage, each time, however, with the special permission of the governors-general, and in localities not subordinate to governors-general - with the permission of the governors"[3]. |
| **[T0101 Censorship January 1876 C0047 The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0101Censorship)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** The censor's refusal to consider national manuscripts: "On a Ukrainian grammar prepared in Russian, the censor wrote the resolution: 'It would be naive to hope for permission to print the grammar of a language that must not exist'"[2]. |
| **[T0010 Denial of a Distinct Identity January 1876 C0047 The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0010Denial of a Distinct Identity)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The ideological justification of the censorship refusal – the language was declared nonexistent by definition: the censor's resolution about "the grammar of a language that must not exist"[2]. |
| **[T0128 Liquidation of National Civic Organizations January 1876 C0047 The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0128Liquidation of National Civic Organizations)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The theater was banned not as repertoire but as an institution: the third point of the 1881 revision prescribed "to completely forbid the establishment of a specifically Little Russian theater and the formation of troupes for performing plays and scenes exclusively in the Little Russian dialect"[3]. Individual plays remained permissible - with administrative permission for each staging. The ban struck not at the text but at the very possibility of a permanent company existing: performing occasionally was allowed, being a Ukrainian theater was not. The report with this point was submitted by the minister of internal affairs Ignatiev; the emperor's assent followed on 8 October 1881[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Ban on the Language in Books and Public Speeches (1892–1905)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Ban on the Language in Books and Public Speeches (1892–1905) (C0049)

A state campaign to drive the language out of public space and literature: in 1892 the Main Administration for Press Affairs directed the censorship committee to suppress translations into Ukrainian, "reducing the number of such talentless works for purely state purposes"[1]; at the archaeological congress in Kyiv in 1899, scholars from Austrian-ruled Ukraine were forbidden to read papers in Ukrainian - in protest they withdrew from participation[2]; at the unveiling of the Kotliarevsky monument in Poltava on 30-31 August 1903, only guests from Galicia were allowed to speak Ukrainian, while the mayor forbade the locals to do so, citing an order of the ministry of internal affairs[2]. Even children's literature fell under the ban: the 1895 circular prohibited Ukrainian books "for children's reading"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0113.001 Legislative Ban on the Native Language January 1892 C0049 Ban on the Language in Books and Public Speeches (1892–1905) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0113.001Legislative Ban on the Native Language)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** The ban on the language in public speech: at the archaeological congress in Kyiv in 1899 the authorities forbade scholars from Austrian-ruled Ukraine to read papers in Ukrainian - they demonstratively withdrew from the sessions[2]. At the unveiling of the Kotliarevsky monument in Poltava on 30-31 August 1903, the Galicians were allowed to speak Ukrainian, but when local Ukrainians began reading a greeting address, the mayor cut the reading short, citing an order of the ministry of internal affairs; only in 1906 did the Senate revoke the ban, even reprimanding the minister for "the impropriety of his actions"[2]. In 1904-1905 the commissions of the Kyiv and Kharkiv universities and the Academy of Sciences, consulted by the Committee of Ministers, spoke out for lifting the bans on the Ukrainian word, yet the decrees of 1876 and 1881 were never formally revoked[2]. |
| **[T0101 Censorship January 1892 C0049 Ban on the Language in Books and Public Speeches (1892–1905) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0101Censorship)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** Total censorship of translations and book imports: in 1892 the Main Administration for Press Affairs directed the censorship committee to suppress translations into Ukrainian, "reducing the number of such talentless works for purely state purposes"[1]; "The ban on importing Ukrainian books from abroad was confirmed in the harshest form in 1894"[3]. |

The censor's resolution on a children's collection: "Obviously written for children, but they must learn in Russian. — Forbid"[3]. |

posts.title: Destruction of Ukrainian Societies and Segregation (1906–1910)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Destruction of Ukrainian Societies and Segregation (1906–1910) (C0050)

A campaign to suppress the legal civic activity of the indigenous people: in the Poltava and Kharkiv regions the "Prosvita" societies were banned from their very founding, and in 1908–1910, under Stolypin, virtually all "Prosvitas" were closed, except the branches of the Katerynoslav governorate[1]. Justifying the crackdown, Stolypin declared in an address to the Senate that the revival of Ukrainian cultural life was undesirable, for "the three principal branches of Eastern Slavdom, both by origin and by language, cannot but constitute one whole"[1]. Stolypin's circular of 1910 classed Ukrainians among the "aliens" and prescribed "to refuse without fail the registration" of their societies[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0128 Liquidation of National Civic Organizations January 1906 C0050 Destruction of Ukrainian Societies and Segregation (1906–1910) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0128Liquidation of National Civic Organizations)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The direct closure of legal educational societies: of the roughly forty "Prosvitas" of Russian-ruled Ukraine, those in the Poltava and Kharkiv regions were banned from their very founding, and in 1908–1910, under Stolypin, virtually all the rest were liquidated, except the branches of the Katerynoslav governorate[1]. The crackdown received its doctrinal grounding: Stolypin declared in an address to the Senate that the revival of Ukrainian cultural life was undesirable, for "the three principal branches of Eastern Slavdom, both by origin and by language, cannot but constitute one whole"[1]. Stolypin's circular to the governors (20 January 1910) — a complete ban on self-organization: "when considering petitions for the registration of any alien societies whatsoever… one must… refuse without fail the registration of their charters"[2]. |
| **[T0032 Legal Segregation of the Population January 1906 C0050 Destruction of Ukrainian Societies and Segregation (1906–1910) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0032Legal Segregation of the Population)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/339):** The official classing of the indigenous population as aliens: Stolypin prescribed to the governors to refuse the registration of "any alien societies whatsoever, including Ukrainian and Jewish ones, regardless of the aims they pursue"[2]. |

posts.title: Ban on Culture and the Press Before World War I (1913–1914)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Ban on Culture and the Press Before World War I (1913–1914) (C0051)

The Russian Empire continued destroying the indigenous people's culture on the eve of the war: the curator of the Kyiv school district, Derevytsky, in 1913 "issued an instruction in which he declared students' attendance of Ukrainian theatrical performances as inadmissible as spending time in billiard halls or beer houses, and in 1914 categorically forbade all educational institutions of the Kyiv district to mark the 100th jubilee of Taras Shevchenko"[1]; with the outbreak of the war, Nicholas II by a personal decree of 20 July 1914 introduced military censorship with the command's right "to suspend periodical publications"[2] - and that very day the military authorities of the Kyiv military district closed the only Ukrainian daily newspaper, "Rada"[3].

---

| Procedures Carried Out |

posts.title: Stalinist Terror and the End of Ukrainization (1922–1939)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Stalinist Terror and the End of Ukrainization (1922–1939) (C0052)

The suppression of the national revival in the USSR: the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the Council of People's Commissars of 14 December 1932, signed by Stalin and Molotov, declared that "Ukrainization was carried out mechanically" and ordered "to immediately transfer in the North Caucasus the record-keeping of the soviet and cooperative bodies of the 'Ukrainized' districts, as well as all published newspapers and journals, from the Ukrainian language to Russian"[1]; the annihilation of most Ukrainian writers of the 1920s-1930s went down in history as the "Executed Renaissance"[2]; the resolution of the USSR Council of People's Commissars and the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 13 March 1938 No. 324 ordered "to introduce the teaching of the Russian language as a subject of study in the schools of the national republics and regions from September 1, 1938"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0120 Extermination Based on Identity January 1922 C0052 Stalinist Terror and the End of Ukrainization (1922–1939) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0120Extermination Based on Identity)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/392):** The targeted physical annihilation of the national cultural elite. The official turn was sealed by the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the Council of People's Commissars "On Grain Procurements in Ukraine, the North Caucasus, and the Western Region" of 14 December 1932, signed by Stalin and Molotov: Ukrainization was declared to have been carried out "mechanically," which, in the resolution's own words, "made it easier for bourgeois-nationalist elements, Petliurites and the like to create their legal covers, their counter-revolutionary cells and organizations"[1]. The term "Executed Renaissance" denotes precisely "the repressive policy of communist Moscow aimed at the physical destruction of the Ukrainian intellectual elite of the 1920s–30s (more broadly – of the entire nationally conscious Ukrainian intelligentsia) and the tabooing of its creative achievements"[2]. |
| **[T0114.001 Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality January 1922 C0052 Stalinist Terror and the End of Ukrainization (1922–1939) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0114.001Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/377):** The compulsory introduction of the metropole's language into schools: the resolution of the USSR Council of People's Commissars and the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 13 March 1938 No. 324 "On the Compulsory Study of the Russian Language in the Schools of the National Republics and Regions" ordered "to introduce the teaching of the Russian language as a subject of study in the schools of the national republics and regions from September 1, 1938" - from the 2nd grade in all non-Russian primary schools and from the 3rd grade in incomplete secondary and secondary schools[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Creation of a Single "Soviet People" (1958–1970)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Creation of a Single "Soviet People" (1958–1970) (C0053)

The USSR's official campaign to erase national distinctions: The start was given by the USSR Law "On Strengthening the Connection of School with Life and on the Further Development of the System of Public Education in the USSR" of December 24, 1958: it contained no direct norm on language, leaving the matter to the republics[1]; the republican Law of the Ukrainian SSR of April 17, 1959, by its Article 9, made the choice of the language of instruction a matter for parents[2]. The Third Program of the CPSU, adopted by the 22nd Congress in October 1961, proclaimed "a new stage in the development of national relations in the USSR, characterized by the further drawing together of nations and the achievement of their complete unity" - up to and including "the effacement of national distinctions, especially of language distinctions"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0114.001 Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality January 1958 C0053 Creation of a Single "Soviet People" (1958–1970) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0114.001Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/377):** The legislative transfer of schools through "freedom of choice": the union Law of December 24, 1958 left the language of instruction to the republics[1], and the Law of the Ukrainian SSR of April 17, 1959 wrote into Article 9: "Instruction in the schools of the Ukrainian SSR is conducted in the pupils' native language. It is for the parents to decide to which school, with which language of instruction, to send their children" - the study of a language not taught in a given school became optional[2]. |
| **[T0158 Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols January 1958 C0053 Creation of a Single "Soviet People" (1958–1970) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0158Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** The material sign of the "merging of nations" was put up in Pereiaslav in the Kyiv region, the city of the Pereiaslav Rada: "on 8 October 1961, a majestic monument in honor of the 300th anniversary of the reunification of Ukraine with Russia was unveiled on B. Khmelnytsky Square"[4]. The authorities unveiled the sign themselves: according to the newsreel Radianska Ukraina No. 49, the opening rally was addressed by Petro Shelest, first secretary of the Kyiv obkom of the CPU, and Pankratov, a secretary of the Moscow obkom of the party - the metropole spoke at the unveiling in its own voice[5]. The composition consisted of two female figures representing Ukraine and Russia and three bas-reliefs with medallions: "a torch, 1654; a hammer and sickle in the rays of the sun, 1917; the Order of Victory, 1945"[6]. The sign's purpose is recorded in its own protection passport: "The monument is a symbol of the eternal, unbreakable friendship and the indestructible monolithic unity of the fraternal peoples - Ukrainian and Russian…"[7]. Four years after the unveiling, the sign was taken under state protection by the resolution of the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR of 21 July 1965 No. 711 "On the approval of the list of monuments of art, history and archaeology of the Ukrainian SSR"[8][9]. The pedestal bore the inscription "Forever together - forever with the Russian people"; in early December 2021 it was removed by unknown persons[10], and the monument itself was dismantled on 7 July 2022 - by an order of the Ministry of Culture that struck the monument, protection No. 5894-Ko, off the register "due to the loss of the subject of protection"[11]. |

</details>

posts.title: Financial Russification of Schools (1978–1983)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Financial Russification of Schools (1978–1983) (C0054)

The Soviet Union introduced a system of direct material incentives for assimilation: pursuant to the resolution of the USSR Council of Ministers of 13 October 1978 No. 835 "On measures for the further improvement of the study and teaching of the Russian language in the union republics," the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR, by its resolution of 2 November 1978 No. 518, introduced the study of Russian from the first grades of Ukrainian schools starting with the 1980/81 school year[1]; the all-Union conference "The Russian Language — the Language of Friendship and Cooperation of the Peoples of the USSR" (Tashkent, 22–24 May 1979) spelled out Russification measures down to kindergartens[2]; the resolution of the CPSU Central Committee and the USSR Council of Ministers of 26 May 1983 No. 473 "On additional measures for improving the study of the Russian language in general-education schools and other educational institutions of the union republics" and the resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Ukraine and the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR of 10 June 1983 raised the salary rates of Russian-language teachers by 15 percent from 1984[2][3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0114.001 Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality January 1978 C0054 Financial Russification of Schools (1978–1983) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0114.001Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/377):** Administrative pressure on schools: pursuant to the resolution of the USSR Council of Ministers of 13 October 1978 No. 835, the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR, by its resolution of 2 November 1978 No. 518, obliged the ministry of education of the Ukrainian SSR to introduce, from the 1980/81 school year, the study of the Russian language in the first grades of general-education schools with Ukrainian as the language of instruction[1]. |
| **[T0115.003 Cultural Chauvinism January 1978 C0054 Financial Russification of Schools (1978–1983) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0115.003Cultural Chauvinism)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/383):** The ideological exaltation of the metropole's language: the all-Union scientific-theoretical conference "The Russian Language — the Language of Friendship and Cooperation of the Peoples of the USSR" adopted detailed recommendations on Russification - from organizing "the study of the Russian language in the senior groups of preschool institutions" to "the use of the Russian language in lessons in other school subjects" in the senior grades of national schools[2]. |
| **[T0114.002 Financial Discrimination Against Teachers January 1978 C0054 Financial Russification of Schools (1978–1983) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0114.002Financial Discrimination Against Teachers)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/378):** Financial privileges for teaching in the metropole's language: pursuant to the resolution of the CPSU Central Committee and the USSR Council of Ministers of 26 May 1983 No. 473 "On additional measures for improving the study of the Russian language in general-education schools and other educational institutions of the union republics," the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Ukraine and the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR, by a resolution of 10 June 1983 - signed by Shcherbytsky and Liashko, stamped "Not for the press" - raised from 1984 by 15 percent the salary rates of teachers of Russian language and literature and allowed classes of more than 25 pupils to be split into subgroups for Russian lessons[2][3]. |

posts.title: Crushing of the Cyril and Methodius Society (1847)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Crushing of the Cyril and Methodius Society (1847) (C0060)

The secret police's blow against the intellectual elite of the indigenous people: "In March 1847 the society was crushed by the gendarmes. The police managed to identify 12 members of the clandestine organization… The tsarist authorities judged the society's program documents a serious threat to the foundations of autocracy"[1]. The sentences for all the accused were proposed by the chief of gendarmes Orlov in his report to the emperor of May 26, 1847, on which Nicholas I inscribed "Execute"[2]. It was accompanied by trials, exiles, and Shevchenko's dispatch into the army "with the institution over the poet of 'the strictest surveillance with a prohibition on writing and drawing'"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0128 Liquidation of National Civic Organizations January 1847 C0060 Crushing of the Cyril and Methodius Society (1847) G0009 Russian Empire S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0128Liquidation of National Civic Organizations)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The destruction of the first political organization of the Ukrainian intelligentsia following student Petrov's denunciation to the secret police: "In March 1847 the society was crushed by the gendarmes. | **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition January 1847 C0060 Crushing of the Cyril and Methodius Society (1847) G0009 Russian Empire S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Arrests, interrogations – the gendarmes "resorted to brutal pressure" and "applied refined methods of psychological processing"[1], and reprisal against the leaders: the sentences were set out in the report of the chief of gendarmes Orlov to the emperor of May 26, 1847, with Nicholas I's resolution "Execute"[2]. Shevchenko was sent into the army "with the institution over the poet of 'the strictest surveillance with a prohibition on writing and drawing'"[3][2]. Hrushevsky: the brotherhood "was seized while still in the midst of its very formation" after a student's denunciation; "The heaviest punishment fell on Shevchenko: he was given over to the soldiery and exiled to the trans-Caspian desert, forbidden to write and to paint," and "persecutions and prohibitions previously unheard of descended upon Ukrainian thought and the Ukrainian word… the very words Ukraine, Little Russia, Hetmanate were deemed criminal"[4]. The brotherhood's co-founder Mykola Hulak "was imprisoned in the Shlisselburg fortress (1847-50), then exiled to Perm under strict police surveillance (1850-59)"[5]. |

</details>

A grueling geopolitical war of the empire, accompanied by the mass mobilization of the Ukrainian peasantry. Nicholas I's manifesto on the state militia and the decrees on its levy of 29 January 1855 (Nos. 28.991–28.993) gave rise to hopes of freedom - even though the Kyiv governorate was not on the list of governorates called up at all[1]: "the movement for re-Cossackization in March–April engulfed over 500 villages and towns in 8 of the 12 districts of the Kyiv governorate… To suppress the 'Cossack movement' the government threw in regular troops and police"[2].

posts.title: Formation of the Ideology of Great-Power Chauvinism (1864–1876)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Formation of the Ideology of Great-Power Chauvinism (1864–1876) (C0063)

Against the backdrop of large-scale territorial conquests, the empire conceptualizes its superiority over the colonized peoples. The ideologue Katkov formulates: "to recognize some element as a distinct nation does not mean granting it freedom, but giving it power, endowing it with binding force. In the recognition of a nation the question of power, of government, of the state is decided"[1] – the recognition of Ukrainians as a nation was ruled out as a question of power.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0003 Cultivation of a Logic of Superiority January 1864 C0063 Formation of the Ideology of Great-Power Chauvinism (1864–1876) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0003Cultivation of a Logic of Superiority)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/313):** The systematic imposition of the metropole's logic of superiority. Researchers reconstruct Katkov's logic thus: "a nation must be a tribe capable of creating a state; only a state nation can establish order in a given territory; tribes incapable of creating a state have to submit to the state nation"[1]. Katkov himself wrote: "In the recognition of a nation the question of power, of government, of the state is decided"[1]. Hrushevsky records both the thesis and its reach: Valuev invoked an imaginary "majority of Little Russians" who allegedly "know neither a Ukrainian nationality nor language, only one Russian people and tongue," while the ideology's mouthpieces carried it to the formula "there are no Ruthenians — there is only one 'Russian people' from the Carpathians to Kamchatka"[2]. |
| **[T0049 Forced Mobilization January 1864 C0063 Formation of the Ideology of Great-Power Chauvinism (1864–1876) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army (T0049Forced Mobilization)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The use of Ukrainians within the imperial army in large-scale wars of conquest in the Caucasus and Central Asia – recruit conscription had extended to the Ukrainian governorates since the liquidation of the autonomy[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Bohdan Khmelnytsky Monument (1888)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Bohdan Khmelnytsky Monument (1888) (C0065)

In 1888 the Russian Empire put up in central Kyiv a monument to Bohdan Khmelnytsky - a sign of the city's belonging to the empire and of "unity" with Moscow. The pedestal bore programmatic inscriptions: "We will to be under the tsar of the east, the Orthodox one" and "To Bohdan Khmelnytsky – one and indivisible Russia"[1]. The monument was unveiled on 11 July 1888 on Sophia Square; the committee for its construction was headed by Mikhail Yuzefovich - an official of the Kyiv educational district and author of the memorandum that formed the basis of the Ems ukase of 1876[1][2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0004 Rewriting of History January 1888 C0065 The Bohdan Khmelnytsky Monument (1888) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0004Rewriting of History)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/314):** On the pedestal of the Khmelnytsky monument (1888) the empire cast a programmatic statement about the past: on the front side stood the phrase "We will to be under the tsar of the east, the Orthodox one," attributed to the Pereiaslav Rada, and on the right - the imperial formula "To Bohdan Khmelnytsky – one and indivisible Russia"[1]. Brought together, they presented the events of 1654 as a voluntary and final choice in favor of a single Russian state, and the entire history of the Hetmanate as the road to that choice. |
| **[T0158 Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols January 1888 C0065 The Bohdan Khmelnytsky Monument (1888) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0158Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** On 11 July 1888 the Russian Empire unveiled the Bohdan Khmelnytsky monument on Sophia Square in Kyiv - a sign of "unity" with Moscow: on the left side of the pedestal stood the dates "1654-1888," counting the city's history from the Pereiaslav Rada[1]. The committee for its construction was headed by Mikhail Yuzefovich[1] - an official of the Kyiv educational district and author of the memorandum that formed the basis of the Ems ukase of 1876[2]. The conference convened over that memorandum, sitting with Yuzefovich's participation, resolved "not to permit the import into the empire, without special authorization of the Main Administration for Press Affairs, of any books or brochures whatsoever published abroad in the Little Russian dialect," and "to forbid the printing and publishing in the empire of original works and translations in that dialect, with the sole exceptions of: a) historical documents and monuments and b) works of belles-lettres" - the latter permitted only in Russian orthography and from a manuscript reviewed by the censorship[3]. Under the decree of the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR of 7 May 1919 on removing from squares and streets the monuments put up to tsars and tsarist minions, two of the three inscriptions were knocked off the pedestal; the remaining one was ordered removed by Hrynko, chairman of the Kyiv gubernia executive committee - academician Yefremov recorded this in his diary on 6 February 1925 - and in the end the side plaques were replaced with blank ones, while "Bohdan Khmelnytskyi 1888" was carved on the front stone[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: All-Russian Census and the Erasure of Identity (1897)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: All-Russian Census and the Erasure of Identity (1897) (C0067)

The empire conducted the general census of 1897, embedded in the doctrine of the "triune Russian people". The linguist Sergei Bulich, in his article for the Brockhaus and Efron Encyclopedic Dictionary, classified Ukrainian speech thus: "the Little Russian dialect of the Russian language"[1]. Historians of the Institute of History of Ukraine of the National Academy of Sciences note: "The census of 1897 recorded not nationality but the respondents' native tongue, and since many Ukrainians named Russian as such, there were in fact more ethnic Ukrainians than indicated in the census"[2]. The census also recorded the reach of the Ukrainian language. According to its consolidated volume, the "Little Russian dialect" - the imperial name for the Ukrainian language - was named as their native tongue by 22,380,551 people out of 125,640,021 counted in the empire, that is 17.8%: the empire's second language by number of speakers after Great Russian (Russian)[3]. Nearly one in four speakers lived outside the nine Ukrainian governorates, and in the Kuban region (now mostly Krasnodar krai of Russia) Ukrainian was the most widespread native language[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (1)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0010 Denial of a Distinct Identity January 1897 C0067 All-Russian Census and the Erasure of Identity (1897) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government (T0010Denial of a Distinct Identity)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The denial to Ukrainians of the status of a separate people at the level of official doctrine. The linguist Sergei Bulich, in the article "Little Russian dialect" of the Brockhaus and Efron Encyclopedic Dictionary (1896), formulated: "The relation of the L[ittle] Russian dialect to the Russian language may be likened to the relation between the Slovak dialect and the Czech language… but not to the relation between the Polish, Czech, Serbian and similar languages, on the one hand, and Russian, on the other"[1] - by this classification Ukrainian was a dialect within the Russian language. This doctrine was applied to the entire empire by the Central Statistical Committee, which conducted the census of 1897: in the tables of the consolidated volume, "Little Russian" ran as a subdivision of a single "Russian language", and its speakers were counted into the overall total of "Russians"[3]. This wrote 22,380,551 people into the "Russians" - speakers of the empire's second language after Great Russian (55,667,469)[3]. Nearly one in four of them - 5,374,863 people - lived outside the nine Ukrainian governorates: in Voronezh governorate 915,883 people named Ukrainian as their native language, in the Don Host region (now mostly Rostov oblast of Russia) - 719,655, in Kursk governorate - 527,778, in Bessarabia (now Moldova and the south of Odesa oblast) - 379,698, in Grodno governorate (now western Belarus) - 362,526, in Stavropol governorate - 319,817, in Lublin and Siedlce governorates (the Kholm region and Podlachia, now eastern Poland) - 304,261, in Siberia - 223,274, of them 54,422 in the Amur and Primorye regions, in Akmolinsk region (now northern Kazakhstan) - 51,103[3]. In the Kuban region Ukrainian was the most widespread native language: 908,818 people declared "Little Russian" (Ukrainian) as their native language against 816,734 with "Great Russian" (Russian), out of a regional population of 1,918,881[3]. The census methodology also undercounted Ukrainians, notes the collective monograph of the Institute of History of Ukraine of the National Academy of Sciences: "The census of 1897 recorded not nationality but the respondents' native tongue, and since many Ukrainians named Russian as such, there were in fact more ethnic Ukrainians than indicated in the census"[2]. |

</details>

He was sent into exile to Simbirsk"[2], then transferred to Kazan with a teaching ban and stripped of his professorship. |

On September 18, 1914, Metropolitan A. Sheptytsky was arrested and taken away to Russia. In all, thousands of Galicians were removed as hostages (through Kyiv alone about 12 thousand passed)"[1]. |

posts.title: Failure of the Political Seizure of the UNR in Kyiv (November – December 1917)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Failure of the Political Seizure of the UNR in Kyiv (November – December 1917) (C0071)

The first attempt by Soviet Russia (the Russian Soviet Republic) to liquidate Ukraine's independence by hijacking power at the All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets. The Bolshevik government (the Sovnarkom) planned to plant its delegates, artificially create a majority, and legally vote to transfer power to the Soviets under its control. The Ukrainian leadership recognized the threat and mobilized its supporters, leaving the aggressor's delegates in an absolute minority and thwarting the takeover[1][2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0131 Support for a Controlled Opposition November 1917 C0071 Failure of the Political Seizure of the UNR in Kyiv (November – December 1917) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0009 Diplomacy (T0131Support for a Controlled Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/403):** Use by the Council of People's Commissars of local Bolshevik cells as a legal political force that was to speak on behalf of the Ukrainian proletariat against the Central Rada[2]. |
| **[T0132 Infiltration of Local Political Structures November 1917 C0071 Failure of the Political Seizure of the UNR in Kyiv (November – December 1917) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0020 Controlled Opposition (T0132Infiltration of Local Political Structures)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/404):** Deliberate transfer of loyal delegates and political agitators to the All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets in Kyiv in order to hijack the agenda from within[1]. |
| **[T0133 Seizure of Power Through Election Manipulation November 1917 C0071 Failure of the Political Seizure of the UNR in Kyiv (November – December 1917) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0020 Controlled Opposition (T0133Seizure of Power Through Election Manipulation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/405):** An attempt to convert an electoral minority into a procedural majority at the congress. Actual support was negligible: in the Constituent Assembly elections "across the country as a whole the Bolsheviks gathered less than 24% of the votes, and in the Ukrainian gubernias only 10%"[1]. Hence the wager on capturing representative bodies: the Central Committee of the RSDLP(b) declared outright that "the transfer of government from the hands of one soviet party into the hands of another party is secured without any revolution, by a simple decision of the Soviets, by a simple re-election of deputies to the Soviets," while the All-Russian Central Executive Committee's decree of 4 December 1917 "On the right of recall of delegates" provided the mechanism for such a replacement[1][3]. |

</details>
