posts.title: Soviet-Ukrainian War: First Invasion and the Puppet Government (December 1917 - April 1918)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Soviet-Ukrainian War: First Invasion and the Puppet Government (December 1917 - April 1918) (C0072)

In December 1917, Soviet Russia began its first armed invasion of Ukraine, disguising it as an internal war. Defeated in Kyiv, supporters of the Bolsheviks moved to Kharkiv, held an alternative congress there, and created a puppet government - the People's Secretariat: "the first Soviet government of Ukraine," created "as an alternative to the Ukrainian Central Rada and the General Secretariat of the Ukrainian Central Rada"[1]. Thus began the Soviet-Ukrainian War (1917-1921): Soviet Russia passed off the invasion by its own troops as an internal civil war[2][3]. In February 1918, RSFSR troops under the command of Muravyov captured Kyiv and carried out a massacre there; historians call Muravyov "the initiator of mass executions in the city"[1]. The invasion was stopped by the Brest-Litovsk peace treaty (9 February 1918) - the first international act to recognize the Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR) as a subject of international law. At the request of the UNR government, German and Austro-Hungarian troops entered Ukraine, and by the end of April 1918 they had driven the RSFSR troops from all Ukrainian land[3]. After Germany's capitulation in November 1918 these troops left - and Soviet Russia invaded again (campaign C0074).

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (5)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0037 Puppet Government December 1917 C0072 Soviet-Ukrainian War: First Invasion and the Puppet Government (December 1917 - April 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations (T0037Puppet Government)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/342):** In December 1917 the Bolsheviks gathered their own congress of soviets in Kharkiv and created a government subordinate to Petrograd, the "People's Secretariat". The goal was to pass off Russia's war against Ukraine as an internal struggle among Ukrainians. The Encyclopedia of the History of Ukraine describes it this way: it was created "as an alternative to the Ukrainian Central Rada and the General Secretariat of the Ukrainian Central Rada" and "acted in close contact with and under the direct leadership of the highest state and party institutions of Soviet Russia"[1]. The congress declared Ukraine a part of Russia. On 12 (25) December 1917 it adopted a resolution on the self-determination of Ukraine. In it the congress recognized "the Ukrainian Republic as a federative part of the Russian Republic" and declared "a resolute struggle against the policy of the Central Rada, ruinous for the worker and peasant masses, exposing its bourgeois, counter-revolutionary character"[4]. The congress explained its right to power by the coup in Petrograd and wrote in the resolution: "the principle of the right of nations to self-determination, proclaimed by the February Revolution, could be put into practice only thanks to the October Revolution, which led to the creation of the Worker-Peasant Government — the Council of People's Commissars"[4]. The puppet government in Kharkiv had no laws of its own: it introduced Petrograd's ready-made decrees in Ukraine. The congress itself decided so: "to immediately extend to the territory of the Ukrainian Republic all decrees and orders of the worker-peasant government of the Federation" and "to declare invalid all orders of the Rada that it has issued and will issue"[5]. The entire new "all-Ukrainian" Soviet authority consisted of 40 people chosen by the congress. There were no peasants among them: the congress left 20 seats for a peasant congress that had not yet convened[6]. Among its first decisions the puppet government appealed to the Council of People's Commissars (the government of Soviet Russia) and annulled the reply of the General Secretariat (the government of the Ukrainian People's Republic under the Central Rada) to Petrograd's ultimatum[6]. It explained the purpose of the appeal this way: "to avoid the possibility of a fratricidal war between the working peoples inhabiting Russia"[6]. The Council of People's Commissars had telegraphed this ultimatum to Kyiv earlier, on 4 (17) December[7]. It put four demands to the Rada. Not to break up the common front by recalling Ukrainian units. Not to let Cossack units pass to the Don, to Kaledin (a general, ataman of the Don Cossack Host, who did not recognize the authority of the Council of People's Commissars), without Petrograd's consent. To help the troops of Soviet Russia against Kaledin. To stop disarming Soviet regiments and the Red Guard. The Council of People's Commissars wrote in the ultimatum: "in the event that a satisfactory answer to these questions is not received within 48 hours, the Council of People's Commissars will consider the Rada to be in a state of open war against Soviet power in Russia and in Ukraine"[8]. The General Secretariat replied with a refusal the next day[7]. The puppet government withdrew that refusal. Thus Petrograd obtained a Ukrainian government that accepted the terms of the ultimatum. Petrograd also kept its own man inside the government. The people's secretary for inter-ethnic affairs, Bakinsky, was at the same time the representative of the Council of People's Commissars of Russia[1]. The historian Stanislav Kulchytsky describes direct supervision: "since no Ukrainian party centre existed, Lenin placed a temporary extraordinary commissar over the Kharkiv government"[9]. That commissar was Ordzhonikidze, an official of the central party apparatus[9]. The journal "Letopis revolyutsii" (a publication of Istpart, the party commission on history) wrote in 1924: "The all-Ukrainian government was a centre without a periphery, a headquarters without an army, when it had neither territory, nor a population subordinate to it, nor an armed force"[10]. |
| **[T0020 Staging a Coup December 1917 C0072 Soviet-Ukrainian War: First Invasion and the Puppet Government (December 1917 - April 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0020Staging a Coup)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/328):** In January 1918, while the troops of Soviet Russia were advancing on Kyiv, the Bolsheviks raised an uprising inside the city itself. On Sunday 15 (28) January, workers and armed Bolshevik detachments seized the "Arsenal" plant in Pechersk (a district of Kyiv)[11]. The next day, 16 (29) January, the Kyiv committee of the Bolshevik party issued a printed leaflet to the workers and soldiers of the city against the General Secretariat. It said: "The gentlemen from the General Secretariat are preparing here, in the heart of Ukraine, the dispersal of the Soviets of Workers' and Soldiers' Deputies and think that soldiers will be found here who will carry out this black deed. No, this shall not be!"[12]. The leaflet called "to the defence of the revolution" and ended with the appeal "Down with the counter-revolutionaries grouped in the Central Rada and the General Secretariat". On 19 January (1 February) Ordzhonikidze, the extraordinary commissar of Soviet Russia in Ukraine, telegraphed the government of Soviet Russia: "In Kyiv there is an uprising of workers and of soldiers of the Bohdan Khmelnytsky and Shevchenko regiments. The Arsenal is in the hands of the workers. Today Soviet troops will enter Kyiv"[13]. The uprising inside the city and the offensive from outside stand in one telegram and in one calculation. |
| **[T0019 Military Intervention December 1917 C0072 Soviet-Ukrainian War: First Invasion and the Puppet Government (December 1917 - April 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0019Military Intervention)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** In January 1918 the troops of Soviet Russia marched on Kyiv. On 16 (29) January Antonov-Ovseyenko, people's commissar for the struggle against counter-revolution in the South, appointed Muravyov commander-in-chief of all Soviet troops acting against the Central Rada[14]. On 17 (30) January, from Bakhmach (a railway junction on the way from Russia to Kyiv), Muravyov reported to the government of Soviet Russia and to Antonov-Ovseyenko: "After a two-day battle the 1st revolutionary army of Yegorov, supported by the 2nd army of Berzin, defeated at Kruty station the counter-revolutionary troops of the Rada, led by Petliura himself", and ended: "I am marching on Kyiv. The peasants greet the revolutionary troops with enthusiasm"[14]. On 21 January (3 February) he told Antonov-Ovseyenko over the direct line: "The revolutionary armies are 20 versts from Darnytsia. For the second day we are moving forward on foot and on carts, since all the bridges have been blown up by the Rada's troops, the tracks are wrecked"[14]. On 25 January (7 February) Muravyov laid out the seizure of the city street by street: "The First Army is to take Fundukleyevska, Volodymyrska, Khreshchatyk and the Merchants' Garden. The Second Army is to take the arsenal, the fortress, Pechersk and all the heights near the fortress and the Lavra. Army commander 2 Berzin is to bring in one or two batteries for street fighting, depending on the situation. Army commander Yegorov is to bring the Bryansk battery into the city"[15]. On 27 January (9 February) he reported to Antonov-Ovseyenko: "At last, after 5 days of fighting in the streets of Kyiv, I have taken possession of the city"[15]. |
| **[T0104 Mass Killings of Civilians December 1917 C0072 Soviet-Ukrainian War: First Invasion and the Puppet Government (December 1917 - April 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0104Mass Killings of Civilians)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** On 22 January (4 February) 1918, five days before the seizure of Kyiv, Muravyov (commander of the Soviet troops acting against the Central Rada of Ukraine) signed order No. 9 at Darnytsia station near Kyiv: "I order the troops of both armies to mercilessly destroy in Kyiv all officers and cadets, Haidamaks, monarchists and all enemies of the revolution. Units that kept neutrality must be immediately disbanded, their property handed over to the Military Revolutionary Committee of the city of Kyiv"[16]. Antonov-Ovseyenko (who commanded the whole expedition into Ukraine) printed this order in his notes together with a reproduction of Muravyov's handwritten original and wrote that the order "at once, by its tone and by its instruction on summary reprisal against all suspicious persons, alarmed our party organization and the Soviet authorities"[15]. On 28 January (10 February) the Kyiv Soviet of Workers' and Soldiers' Deputies (the organ of that very Soviet power which the troops had brought) resolved: "The Soviet expresses its resolute condemnation of the unceasing lynchings of prisoners, which stain the glorious victory of the proletariat. Those who have disgraced themselves by the murder of the unarmed must be expelled from the ranks of the socialist army and handed over to a revolutionary court. Enough violence!"[17]. On 19 March 1918 members of the committee of the 1st revolutionary army came with a complaint against Muravyov to Dzerzhinsky, head of the Cheka, the Bolsheviks' secret police[18]. On 5 May Dzerzhinsky testified to the investigative commission: "our worst enemy could not have done us as much harm as he did with his nightmarish reprisals, executions, tyranny, and by granting the soldiers the right to plunder towns and villages. All this he did in the name of our Soviet power, turning the whole population against us. Plunder and violence — that was his deliberate military tactic"[18]. Muravyov himself, from prison on the same day, 5 May, conveyed the accusation this way: "no charge has been brought against me, apart from a verbal one 'for plunder, drunkenness and murders'"[19]. On 9 June 1918 the presidium of the All-Russian Central Executive Committee, the highest organ of Soviet power, on the report of Krylenko from the investigative commission, closed the case for absence of a crime[18]. Mykhailo Hrushevsky, head of the Central Rada, wrote about the commander in 1921: "the chief commandant, the former gendarme Muravyov, back in February boasted of shooting Ukrainians and of ruining their property"[20]. |
| **[T0109 Sham Expression of Popular Will December 1917 C0072 Soviet-Ukrainian War: First Invasion and the Puppet Government (December 1917 - April 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0020 Controlled Opposition (T0109Sham Expression of Popular Will)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/369):** In December 1917 the Bolsheviks held a sham "all-Ukrainian" congress in Kharkiv to give the seizure of power in Ukraine the appearance of an expression of the people's will. The elected assemblies of workers and soldiers, through which the Bolsheviks were trying to seize power, gathered at the real All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets in Kyiv on 4–6 (17–19) December 1917. At the real congress Ukrainians hardly noticed the Bolsheviks: of more than 2,500 delegates "the Bolsheviks were represented by only 150", and the congress supported the Central Rada[3]. The communists decided not to give up. Zatonsky (one of them, later a member of the puppet government in Kharkiv) recalled: "having gathered illegally in the premises of the trade unions, the delegates of the congress, all Bolsheviks except for two or three Left SRs, resolved to declare themselves the plenipotentiary Congress of Soviets of the Country, to elect a Central Executive Committee and a government of Soviet Ukraine and, having moved to Kharkiv, to take up open struggle against the Central Rada"[21]. The new "congress" met in a city already seized by Russian troops. The historian Stanislav Kulchytsky writes: "the day before the opening of the congress of soviets the Central Rada's garrison in Kharkiv was disarmed by the troops of V. Antonov-Ovseyenko, whom the Council of People's Commissars had instructed to take Ukraine by force of arms"[9]. On 9 (22) December the regional congress of soviets of the Donbas and Kryvyi Rih area opened in Kharkiv. When the delegates' credentials were checked, 77 people with the right to vote and another 6 without it were counted. In the Donbas and the Kryvyi Rih area there were 140 elected assemblies of workers and soldiers, and only 46 of them had sent delegates. By the rule of the previous regional congress, a session was allowed only with delegates from half of these assemblies. Those gathered in Kharkiv abolished this rule by a vote of 46 to 18 with 5 abstentions and declared themselves entitled to sit. Then the delegates who had left Kyiv addressed the gathering. By a majority of 43 to 11 the assembly resolved "to merge with the representatives of the Regional Congress and to name the congress 'the Congress of Soviets of Workers' and Soldiers' Deputies of Ukraine with the participation of part of the peasant deputies'"[22]. Thus an assembly of one region began to speak in the name of all Ukraine. It granted itself the right to sit by abolishing its own rule that a session was allowed only with delegates from at least half of the region's assemblies. Its new name came from a vote of 43 to 11 in a Kharkiv hall, not from elections: outside the hall nobody had voted for this congress. The historian Vladyslav Verstiuk calls it "a hastily staged alternative congress of soviets": "at it 89 soviets and military revolutionary committees were represented by 200 delegates", whereas "soviets alone at that moment numbered more than 300 in Ukraine"[23]. The historian Larysa Yakubova notes: there were "almost no" peasant delegates, and Soviet historiography later scrubbed the qualifier "with the participation of peasant deputies" from the congress's name[2]. In the resolution of 9 (22) December that qualifier stands[22]. The majority of Ukraine's population remained outside the doors of the hall. The assembly declared itself the All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets and proclaimed the creation of a Soviet - "supposedly truly people's" - Ukrainian People's Republic[2]. |

</details>

# Campaign: Artificial Separatism and the Dismemberment of Territories (January – March 1918) (C0073)

Having been forced to recognize Ukraine's independence under the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, the government of Soviet Russia attempted to retain control over the eastern industrial regions. To this end, a separate separatist entity (the Donetsk–Kryvyi Rih Soviet Republic) was artificially constructed on the territory of the Donbas and the Kryvyi Rih region, with the aim of directly subordinating these lands to the central Russian authorities, bypassing the UNR[1][2].

posts.title: Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) (C0074)

After Germany's capitulation in World War I, the German and Austro-Hungarian troops that had occupied Ukraine since the spring of 1918 left[1] - and in January 1919 RSFSR troops invaded Ukraine for the second time: the Soviet-Ukrainian War went on[1]. The cover had been prepared in advance: as early as 28 November 1918, the Central Committee of the Bolshevik party (CC RCP(b)) created a "Provisional Workers' and Peasants' Government of Ukraine" in the Russian city of Kursk to provide political cover for the invasion[2]. The goal was the resources of the captured land: the head of the RSFSR government, Lenin, advised Petrograd workers to go to Ukraine for provisions and fuel - "It is foolish to starve and perish in Petrograd when you can win back bread and coal"[3]. The villages answered the grain seizures with uprisings, and the Russian command treated the war against them as frontline work[4]. In the summer of 1919 a second Russian army came to Ukraine - the Armed Forces of South Russia under General Denikin (the "Whites"), who likewise denied Ukrainian statehood[5]. On 30 August 1919 Ukrainian troops took Kyiv, abandoned by the Bolsheviks, but on 31 August the Whites pushed them out - the day went down in history as the "Kyiv Catastrophe"[6]. By the autumn of 1919 the Whites had driven out the RSFSR troops and established their military dictatorship over most of Ukraine[7]. In December 1919 Soviet Russia invaded for the third time (campaign C0104).

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (21)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0019 Military Intervention January 1919 C0074 Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0019Military Intervention)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** A full-scale offensive by the Ukrainian Front of the Red Army in early 1919 to recapture Ukrainian cities after the withdrawal of Austro-German troops[8].⏎In the summer of 1919 Ukraine was also under attack by the White army - the Armed Forces of South Russia led by General Denikin[5]. The advance of Denikin's White army on Kyiv ran under the slogan of restoring a "united and indivisible Russia"[8]. On August 30, 1919, Kyiv, abandoned by the Reds almost without a fight, was taken by the combined Ukrainian forces - the 1st and 3rd corps of the Ukrainian Galician Army (UHA) and the Zaporizhzhia Group of the army of the Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR) under the overall command of the Galician general Kravs; for 4 p.m. the next day, Sunday, August 31, Kravs scheduled a ceremonial parade of the Ukrainian troops on Khreshchatyk with the participation of Symon Petliura, head of the UNR Directory[9]. The day after the Ukrainian armies entered the capital, Kyiv was also occupied by Denikin's troops under General Bredov, who forced the Ukrainian units out[9]. The events of August 31, 1919 became known as the "Kyiv catastrophe"[9][8]. A catastrophe this day was for the Ukrainian armies and for the statehood of the UNR: they lost the capital, taken the day before, within a single day; the armed clash on Duma Square left dead and wounded, and several hundred men were taken prisoner[9]. Historians of the Institute of History of Ukraine of the National Academy of Sciences conclude: "the initially successful operation of the Ukrainian forces turned into a painful defeat". Of the consequences they write: the catastrophe "had a demoralizing effect on the Ukrainian army and deepened the divergence in the strategic aims" of the two Ukrainian political leaderships - that of Dnieper Ukraine and that of Galicia[9].⏎The course of the day is known from the diary of the Supreme Command - the staff of the Ukrainian Galician Army. The staff described the morning of August 31 thus: at 8 o'clock Denikin's units entered the city, "it seems - across the middle unoccupied bridge and also across the railway bridge, over which several armored trains crossed", and positioned themselves in the southeastern suburbs[10]. The senior Galician commander, Otaman Vimetal, agreed with Denikin's commanders on a provisional demarcation line, but between 4 and 5 p.m. Denikin's general Stackelberg, with a delegation of officers and a detachment of 100-200 men, approached the City Duma, already held by the Galicians; Kravs demanded that they be withdrawn behind the agreed line[10]. The staff recorded the denouement thus: the assembled crowd, "knowing of the presence of Denikin's troops in Kyiv, demanded that the Russian flag be hung on the Duma in addition to the Ukrainian one we had already planted there", and Kravs, "in order to calm the crowd, in which there were many former Russian officers", permitted it with the justification "as a banner of the common struggle of both armies against the Bolsheviks"[10]. Units of the Zaporizhzhia Group passing by the Duma "tore down the Russian flag"; shooting broke out - Denikin's detachments attacked the Galician units scattered across the city, and of the fire from roofs and balconies the diary entry reads: "the civilian population also fired at our units"[10]. The day's toll in the diary: "10 Cossacks killed", the disarmed staff of the III Galician Corps and eleven of its companies, the guns of the Zaporizhzhia Group abandoned in the city; Kravs estimated Denikin's forces at "at least two divisions"[10]. There was no battle for the city: after the shooting at the Duma "great panic" set in - several units were disarmed, the rest fought their way out of the city; the staff summed up: "a unified resistance was impossible because of the panic mentioned"[10]. Kravs set out to negotiate with Bredov and already on his way met "strong columns of volunteers [soldiers of Denikin's Volunteer Army]" marching on the city[10].⏎Kyiv remained with Denikin's forces. On the night of September 1 Kravs signed with Bredov an agreement on the withdrawal of the Galician units; by September 2 the group's troops were already assembling on the Ihnativka - Vasylkiv line[10]. The withdrawal was the command's decision: the riflemen of the group, according to the entry for September 1, "deeply dispirited by the recent events, demand a new offensive on Kyiv"[10].⏎In the fall of 1919 the Red Army went over to a counteroffensive, now against Denikin's forces[8]. |
| **[T0052 Expropriation of Resources January 1919 C0074 Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0052Expropriation of Resources)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** Mezhlauk, deputy war minister of the Soviet colonial administration of Ukraine (the UkrSSR), telegraphed Lenin on 5 April 1919: Ukraine must not be looked upon "as a promised land" of inexhaustible reserves - its resources had to be counted among the all-Russian ones as soon as possible and used under a single plan[11]. In the second half of April 1919 Lenin, head of the RSFSR government, proposed that the Petrograd organizations ship workers to Ukraine to replenish stocks of food and fuel: "Continue the mobilization of workers in Piter, extending it to Ukraine and the Don... I advise sending these workers en masse to Ukraine, the Don, the East for 3 months. It is foolish to starve and perish in Piter when bread and coal can be won back"[3]. By a decree of 12 April 1919 this administration obliged every village to hand over to the state the amount of grain assigned to it[12]. The grain was taken from Ukrainians by the administration's food ministry: it sent armed workers' detachments into the villages, and alongside them the grain was seized by detachments of the Bolsheviks' secret police - the extraordinary commissions (Cheka) - and by units of the Russian army[12]. These detachments confiscated peasants' property and implements, took hostages, and made a whole village answer for a single inhabitant. Detachments of the same ministry and of the Cheka intercepted, on roads and at railway stations, Ukrainians carrying grain for barter or sale outside the state monopoly: the food was seized, and carrying grain was punished up to and including execution[12]. Refusing to hand over property cost lives: in June 1919 agents of the Kherson district extraordinary commission detained Nykyfor Potachenko, a 24-year-old peasant of the village of Roksandrivka in Kherson district, "for unwillingness to provide horses"; by the commission's resolution he was shot on the night of 15 June (a local history publication gives 15 July) in the basement of the Tyulpanov house - twice he climbed out of the filled-in grave alive, and only the third execution killed him[13]. On 14 June 1919 Lenin telegraphed Kyiv at three addresses at once - Rakovsky, head of the colonial administration, Shlikhter, its food minister, and Podvoisky, its war minister - shifting the supply of the Russian fronts onto Ukrainian grain: "In view of the utter impossibility of provisioning the Western and Northern fronts from the exhausted stocks of the Centre, the whole weight of this state task naturally passes to the delegation of Tsekomprodarm, led by Orlov and working under Trotsky's order for the entire Russian army as a whole"; in the same telegram he demanded that the administration's war ministry assist this delegation "so that it can immediately move food freight to the armies of the West and North"[14]. A week later, on 21 June, Lenin sent Rakovsky a telegram marked "out of all turn" and "with verification of the exact time of delivery," setting a deadline: "The Western army absolutely needs three trainloads of bread within the coming days. I urgently request the most energetic measures to meet this need. The extremity is utmost"[15]. |
| **[T0036 Installation of a New System of Governance January 1919 C0074 Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations (T0036Installation of a New System of Governance)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** On 1 June 1919 the central Soviet authority of Russia (the VTsIK) resolved to carry out "a close unification of 1) the military organization and military command, 2) the councils of the national economy, 3) railway administration and management, 4) finances and 5) the commissariats of labour" of Russia, Ukraine, Latvia, Lithuania, Belarus and Crimea - "so that the direction of the said branches of national life be concentrated in the hands of single collegiums." The resolution was signed by Kalinin, chairman of the VTsIK, and by secretary Serebryakov, while preserving the formula of independence word for word: the unification was carried out "standing fully on the ground of recognition of the independence, freedom and self-determination of the toiling masses of Ukraine, Latvia, Lithuania, Belarus and Crimea"[16]. Ukraine's economy, railways, finances and labour passed under Moscow's management; independence remained a word on paper. The food ministry was not on that list: Lenin, head of the RSFSR government, subordinated it separately and in secret. On 12 June 1919 he sent a note to Kyiv: the food ministry of the colonial administration of Ukraine was passing under the all-Russian one in both money and management - without any announcement; at the bottom of the note stood the instruction to encipher the underlined part and transmit it immediately, and on 14 June the question was put before the plenum of the Central Committee of the Bolshevik party[17]. |
| **[T0022 Terror January 1919 C0074 Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0022Terror)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** In captured Kyiv the occupiers shot hundreds of people over 1919: they killed at night, printed the names of the dead daily in a newspaper, and in the last week of August proclaimed a "week of red terror." An eyewitness - Kateryna Koval-Medzvedska, a Kyivan who lived seven months in the city under Moscow's occupation, from February to August 1919 - recorded that on 24 August 1919 "a 'week of red terror' was officially proclaimed - blood flowed in rivers. Peters, Voroshilov and Latsis, all-powerful that day, took no account of government members Rakovsky, Manuilsky and others who signed orders for releases from the Cheka, but ordered those people shot 'in the order of red terror.'" The shooting was done at night: "From 2 to 4 o'clock the sinister night silence of the unhappy, tormented city was broken by single shots and the piercing sounds of a car siren. People living near one of the 17 chekas scattered across the city understood that our brothers were being shot, their cries and groans drowned out by the red executioners with the shrill piercing sounds of sirens"[18]. From 24 to 30 August inclusive the newspaper Izvestia - the organ of the Kyiv occupation authority - daily announced lists of dozens shot "in the order of red terror"; on 26 August "a list was announced of 167 persons shot 'in the order of red terror'" - among them people whose release order the eyewitness had read two days earlier in the chancellery of the central organ of the colonial administration (the VUTsIK). "And how many people perished without announcement, simply vanished without trace!"[18]. One of those newspaper lists survived in a reprint: Shumakher, acting head of the Whites' Information Section, reproduced in "Summary of Information on the Atrocities and Lawlessness of the Bolsheviks" No. 25 a list printed in the Kyiv Izvestia of people shot by the occupiers: a professor, a gymnasium teacher, merchants, house-owners, attorneys, former Kyiv governor Sukovkin, former vice-governor Neklyudov, 80-year-old Slynko[13]. The very form of the announcements came from Moscow: the RSFSR government's resolution "On Red Terror" of 5 September 1918, signed by justice minister Kursky and interior minister Petrovsky, required "publishing the names of all those shot, as well as the grounds for applying this measure to them" - the Kyiv lists with the formula "in the order of red terror" delivered names and grounds, exactly what the resolution demanded[19]. The head of the Soviet colonial administration of Ukraine, Rakovsky, wrote to Lenin on 9 August 1919 that the Kyiv secret police had been carried away with executions by hastily drawn-up lists and that more than 300 people had been shot in Kyiv in total[20], while Latsis, chairman of the Ukrainian secret police, gave his own statistics in his 1920 report book: "Shot by the Kyiv Extraordinary Commission jointly with the V.U.Ch.K. - 825" people in 1919 up to October[21]. |
| **[T0120 Extermination Based on Identity January 1919 C0074 Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0014 White Movement (AFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0120Extermination Based on Identity)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/392):** Units of the Volunteer Army captured the town of Fastiv in Kyiv province on 25 August 1919 (7 September by the modern calendar) - and on the same day began robbing the inhabitants of the town's Jewish quarters. Pakhomov, the Whites' temporary commandant, having received 25,000 roubles from a Jewish delegation, promised to take measures but refused to stop the violence at once, explaining why: "since the troops are greatly embittered against the Jews." The Whites' garrison was commanded by Belogortsev. The Whites killed on a schedule: "Towards evening all the Cossacks, regulars and partisans separately, were usually assembled for roll-call. After roll-call and prayer they scattered in groups across the town 'to work.'" Those fleeing were caught on the railway: "Many were taken off trains along the way and led into the forest to be shot"[22]. When a Russian delegation came to the commandant asking him to stop the pogrom, because the Russian population had begun to suffer from it too, he asked: "And who is doing the robbing?" - and, on hearing that the Russian population was also taking part, replied: "And later they will say it was the Cossacks who robbed"[22]. On 23 September 1919 Kundo, the Whites' commandant in Fastiv, issued order No. 2 declaring everything settled: "I add that measures for the protection of order in the townlet were taken long ago, all apprehensions are entirely groundless. Of all cases of robbery, violence and requisitions I request immediate notification to the commandant's office"[23]. Rabinovich, a commissioner of the Russian Red Cross, described the result of the three days thus: "The pogrom, like a tornado, destroyed, burned and scattered the greater half of the town... From the smouldering ruins of the fires bodies of those burned in the houses were still being recovered"[24]. By 30 September 1919, 600 killed, 100 burned and 315 wounded had been counted in Fastiv - out of eight thousand Jewish inhabitants of the town, and the figure was incomplete: "there are far more killed, since to this day bodies are being found in the woods"[22]. |
| **[T0077 Punitive Expeditions January 1919 C0074 Soviet-Ukrainian War: Second Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army (T0077Punitive Expeditions)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/359):** The resistance of the villages of captured Ukraine tied down troops for the whole of 1919. On 18 April 1919 Antonov-Ovseenko, commander of the RSFSR's Ukrainian Front, reported to Vatsetis, commander-in-chief of the RSFSR armed forces, that he would give no troops for the Southern Front: "Right now there is hard fighting at Shepetivka and Tiraspol and a hard struggle with kulak uprisings everywhere." Vatsetis wrote on the report: "Carry out the order and report back"[4]. Two weeks later, on 3 May 1919, Antonov-Ovseenko repeated his refusal and named the scale: "30 versts from Kyiv there is a kulak uprising, up to three thousand well-armed men with 8 guns." Vatsetis answered as before: "I repeat that the order must be carried out"[25]. For the command, the Ukrainian peasants who had risen against the seizures were not an adversary but a hindrance to supplying the front: it regarded the Ukrainian village as a rear area to be kept in order while the main forces carried out Moscow's tasks. Naval artillery was turned on the risen villages too: on 2-5 May 1919 the armed steamers of the Dnipro river flotilla shelled Chornobyl, Pliuty and Trypillia, held by the insurgents - the vessels "Arnold," "Verny" and "Admiral" are named in the operational summary one by one[26]. On 25 May 1919, summing up for the armies of the front the fighting against the Ukrainian units of commander Hryhoriv, who had risen against the Soviet authority, Antonov-Ovseenko laid down the order of the mopping-up: those who surrendered were to be handed to the military tribunals of the Soviet authority, "ringleaders and chiefs" singled out separately, and the villages in the armies' areas of operation disarmed with the taking of hostages; the order was signed with him by commissar Savitsky and chief of staff Babin[27]. |

# Campaign: Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) (C0075)

The final destruction of Ukrainian sovereignty through the imposition of treaties on a so-called military-political union. While formally preserving the status of an independent republic, the leadership of the RSFSR de facto brought the key Ukrainian agencies — military, financial, economic, and transport — under its direct control. On March 18, 1921, Soviet Russia and Soviet Ukraine signed the Treaty of Riga with Poland and divided the Ukrainian lands. Poland, the ally of the Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR) under the Treaty of Warsaw, signed peace with Soviet Ukraine, recognizing it as a state[1][2][3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (6)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0088 Sham Treaties June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0009 Diplomacy (T0088Sham Treaties)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/360):** Use of the "union treaty" format of June 1, 1919, and December 28, 1920, not to create an equal federation but as an instrument for legalizing direct, rigid rule from Moscow[2]. |
| **[T0031 Restriction of Sovereignty June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0009 Diplomacy (T0031Restriction of Sovereignty)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Transfer of control over the military affairs, finances, communications, and transport routes of the Ukrainian republic into the hands of the central bodies of the RSFSR[2]. |
| **[T0008 Deprivation of Agency June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0009 Diplomacy (T0008Deprivation of Agency)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** De facto liquidation of the Ukrainian army (the disbandment of the Ukrainian Front) and the transformation of the government of the Ukrainian SSR into a nominal appendage of the Russian administrative machine[2]. |
| **[T0039 Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0009 Diplomacy (T0039Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The signing of the Treaty of Riga in March 1921: a backroom division of spheres of influence and Ukrainian territories with Poland behind the back of the Ukrainian people, legalized through the formal participation of the puppet Ukrainian SSR[3]. |
| **[T0036 Installation of a New System of Governance June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0036Installation of a New System of Governance)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** Moscow's seizure of direct control over the punitive apparatus through the decision to liquidate the independent All-Ukrainian Cheka (VUChK) in August 1919 and the appointment of its own special commissar, Ya. Peters[2]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0008 Government (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Coercion of legal Ukrainian parties into self-dissolution (in particular, the Borotbists in the spring of 1920) and their absorption by the CP(b)U through political blackmail and the bribery of their leaders with official posts[2]. |

# Campaign: Legal Absorption through the Creation of the USSR (1922–1924) (C0076)

Formal consolidation of the seizure of Ukraine by dragging it into the so-called Union of SSRs. The unification of equal republics with the right of free secession was declared, but in practice the union treaty (December 1922) and the Constitution of the USSR (1924) became instruments of rigid centralization. The Ukrainian SSR was definitively stripped of control over foreign policy, the army, foreign trade, transport, and communications — all these spheres passed to the jurisdiction of union-level people's commissariats in Moscow[1][2].

---

posts.title: Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932) (C0077)

An assault on the traditional way of life of the Ukrainian village, which remained the principal bearer of national identity and economic independence. Under the slogans of socialist modernization, Moscow proclaimed the course of "the liquidation of the kulaks as a class": the secret Politburo resolution of January 30, 1930 ordered "to confiscate from the kulaks of these districts the means of production, livestock, farm and residential buildings, processing enterprises, fodder and seed stocks" and to send "60,000 to concentration camps and subject 150,000 kulaks to deportation to remote districts," of which for Ukraine - 15 thousand to concentration camps and 30–35 thousand to deportation[1]. Peasants who put up resistance were dispossessed en masse and deported to Siberia and the North[2].

---

| **[T0038 Economic Control January 1928 C0077 Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0038Economic Control)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/343):** Forcible seizure of land, livestock, and agricultural implements from peasants as part of forced collectivization under slogans of socialist modernization[2]. |

| **[T0127 Deportation January 1928 C0077 Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0127Deportation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/399):** Mass deportation of hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian peasants ("kulaks") and their family members to Siberia and remote northern regions of the USSR[2]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition January 1928 C0077 Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Mass arrests of peasants during the dekulakization campaign: according to the 1930 directives, in addition to deportations, tens of thousands of people were sent directly to concentration camps for isolation[2]. |

posts.title: Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) (C0078)

The use of artificial famine as a weapon of mass destruction for the physical and psychological suppression of national resistance. The launch of a merciless grain-procurement machine, the confiscation of absolutely all food, the introduction of the "blackboard" regime (a total blockade of settlements)[1], and a ban prohibiting peasants from leaving the starving districts: the directive of Stalin and Molotov of January 22, 1933 ordered "not to allow the mass departure of peasants from Ukraine to other regions," declaring the flight of the starving "for bread" a plot "organized by enemies of Soviet power, SRs and agents of Poland"[2]. Physical extermination was accompanied by total psychological terror and show trials[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (6)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0121 Artificial Famine August 1932 C0078 Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0121Artificial Famine)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/393):** Confiscation of absolutely all food, including the extraction of seed stocks, through the mechanism of crushing grain procurement quotas, which led to mass deadly famine[3]. |
| **[T0108 Economic Blockade August 1932 C0078 Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) G0010 USSR S0010 Regular Army (T0108Economic Blockade)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/368):** The introduction of the "blackboard" regime - a total economic blockade of settlements. The resolution of the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR and the CC of the CP(b)U of December 6, 1932, signed by Chubar and Kosior, prescribed "the immediate cessation of the delivery of goods, the complete cessation of cooperative and state trade on site, and the removal of all available goods from the respective cooperative and state shops," as well as "a complete ban on kolkhoz trade both for kolkhozes and kolkhoz members and for individual farmers"[1]. |
| **[T0104 Mass Killings of Civilians August 1932 C0078 Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0104Mass Killings of Civilians)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** Deliberately starving millions of Ukrainian peasants to death as a direct result of Moscow's state policy[3]. |
| **[T0022 Terror August 1932 C0078 Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0022Terror)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Systematic psychological suppression through public show trials of "saboteurs" and the introduction of the punitive law on the protection of socialist property (the "law of five ears of grain")[3]. |
| **[T0107 Transport Blockade August 1932 C0078 Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0107Transport Blockade)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/367):** Sealing off the starving region: peasants who tried to escape from the blockaded villages were intercepted on roads and at railway junctions. The directive sealed off precisely Ukraine and the Kuban: "all peasants who had managed to leave Ukraine and the North Caucasus were subject to return to their places of residence," while permits to leave were denied even "to the national districts of the krai, where there was no famine at all"[3]. Within 50 days "219.5 thousand peasants were detained, including 38 thousand in the Ukrainian SSR, 47 thousand in the North Caucasus, 44 thousand in the Central Black Earth region, 5 thousand in the Western oblast, 65 thousand on the railways"; of these, "186.5 thousand were sent home under convoy, almost 3 thousand were convicted, and all the rest awaited trial or were under investigation in filtration camps"[3]. The point of the operation lay not in sentences but in marching people back into the starving villages: the coded telegram "documentarily attests to his intention to organize absolute famine in the rural areas of Ukraine"[3]. |
| **[T0057 Labor Exploitation August 1932 C0078 Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0057Labor Exploitation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** Lethally dangerous exploitation of the labor of Ukrainian peasants, convicted en masse under the "law of five ears of grain" and exiled to corrective labor camps during the Holodomor[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) (C0079)

The abrupt rollback of the policy of "Ukrainization." The start of the physical extermination and political defamation of the intellectual elite - writers, scholars, film directors, as well as the old national communists (M. Skrypnyk was driven to suicide)[1]. In parallel with the physical terror came the destruction of the Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church, large-scale censorship, the rewriting of history, and the artificial convergence of the Ukrainian language with Russian; works published in the Ukrainian SSR before 1933, in the words of the compiler of the anthology "Executed Renaissance," were "destroyed as a result of Moscow's new course toward the rout and colonial provincialization of Ukraine"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0022 Terror January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0022Terror)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Creation of an atmosphere of total paralyzing fear in society through the fabrication of cases (for example, the "Union for the Liberation of Ukraine") and the staging of public show trials[1]. |
| **[T0101 Censorship January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0101Censorship)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** Mass confiscation and destruction of literature declared "nationalist," and rigid control over the printed word and the arts[1]. |
| **[T0113 Linguistic Assimilation January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0113Linguistic Assimilation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/373):** The forced orthography reform of 1933, aimed at artificially bringing Ukrainian grammar and terminology closer to the Russian language[1]. |
| **[T0100 Seizure of Religious Institutions January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0100Seizure of Religious Institutions)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/362):** Mass closure and destruction of churches, as well as repressions against clergy, aimed at the complete destruction of the Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church (UAOC)[1]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Physical annihilation and isolation of the Ukrainian intelligentsia, writers, and scholars, as well as of the party opposition (national communists), in the course of targeted repressions. Fabrication of cases (including the "UNC" case) and driving representatives of the national elite to death, including the historian Mykhailo Hrushevsky, the writer Mykola Khvylovy, and People's Commissar Mykola Skrypnyk[1]. |
| **[T0045 Destruction of Historical Memory January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0045Destruction of Historical Memory)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/349):** Institutional destruction of national historical scholarship, closure of research schools, and removal of the works of Ukrainian historians from scholarly circulation[1]. |
| **[T0004 Rewriting of History January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0021 Propaganda (T0004Rewriting of History)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/314):** The construction of a new Soviet-imperial historical canon to supplant the Ukrainian past: "from the late 1930s a thesis took hold in the historical scholarship of the USSR," proclaimed in the works of B. Grekov, K. Huslystyi, and F. Yastrebov, "of Kyivan Rus as the 'common cradle' of the history of the Ukrainian, Russian, and Belarusian peoples," and "in 1939 B. Grekov advanced the proposition of the ethnic unity of the 'Rus people' in the era of Kyivan Rus"[3]. This scheme displaced M. Hrushevsky's conception and denied the independence of Ukraine's history. |

</details>

posts.title: NKVD National Operations and Institutional Russification (1937–1939)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: NKVD National Operations and Institutional Russification (1937–1939) (C0080)

The total purge of ethnic minorities (Poles, Germans, Greeks, Bulgarians) during the Great Terror through targeted national orders of the NKVD. In parallel, in 1938, Moscow officially liquidated every single national district and minority school - by resolutions of the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 24 January 1938[1][2] - and by the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the USSR Council of People's Commissars of 13 March 1938 No. 324 made the study of the Russian language compulsory[3]; Kyiv executed the decision by the resolution of the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U of 10 April 1938[4], returning to overtly imperial practices of assimilation[5][6].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0120 Extermination Based on Identity August 1937 C0080 NKVD National Operations and Institutional Russification (1937–1939) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0120Extermination Based on Identity)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/392):** The conduct of secret mass "national operations" of the NKVD for the physical annihilation of members of ethnic minorities[6]. The mechanism was set by the operational orders of people's commissar Yezhov: No. 00485 of 11 August 1937 opened the Polish operation - "to begin, from 20 August 1937, a broad operation aimed at the complete liquidation of the local organizations of the 'POW'" with completion "within a three-month term"[7], - and No. 00439 of 25 July 1937 the German one[8]; the Greek, Bulgarian and other operations followed their template[6]. The scale is recorded in the perpetrator's own accounting: according to the summary figures of the 1st Special Department of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR dated 30 August 1938, 94,659 people were arrested in the republic under orders Nos. 00485, 00593 and others (54,011 on the Polish line, 23,036 on the German, 5,642 on the Greek), of whom 61,683 had been convicted by 1 July 1938; in all, of the 197,945 people convicted by the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR over the reporting period, 122,274 were sentenced to be shot - nearly two out of every three[9]. Across all the "national lines" of the USSR, 335,513 people were convicted, and 73.66% of them were shot[10]. |
| **[T0128 Liquidation of National Civic Organizations August 1937 C0080 NKVD National Operations and Institutional Russification (1937–1939) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0128Liquidation of National Civic Organizations)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The forcible closure of all national councils, pedagogical institutes, theaters and cultural institutions of ethnic minorities in the Ukrainian SSR[5]: the national districts and village soviets were liquidated by the resolution of the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 24 January 1938[2], and the resolution of the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U of 10 April 1938 reorganized the national schools and colleges and turned the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute into an institute of foreign languages[4]. |
| **[T0114.003 Conversion of Schools to the Metropole's Language August 1937 C0080 NKVD National Operations and Institutional Russification (1937–1939) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0114.003Conversion of Schools to the Metropole's Language)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/379):** On 24 January 1938 the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b), by its resolution "On the Liquidation of National Schools and National Sections in Schools," closed non-Russian schools throughout the Union, liquidating the national districts and village soviets on the same day[1][2]; on 13 March the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the USSR Council of People's Commissars No. 324 "On the Compulsory Study of the Russian Language in the Schools of the National Republics and Regions" made the metropole's language a compulsory subject in all schools of the republics[3]. Kyiv executed the decision on 10 April 1938: the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U, "proceeding from the decision of the Central Committee of the VKP(b)," declared "the further existence of special national schools inexpedient and harmful" and resolved to reorganize the German, Polish, Czech, Swedish and other schools and technical colleges "into Soviet schools of the ordinary type," to liquidate national sections and classes at ordinary schools, colleges and universities, and, where there was nowhere to transfer the pupils, to transfer the institutions themselves to ordinary school curricula - "with instruction in Ukrainian or Russian"; the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute was turned into an institute of foreign languages, and all the work was ordered finished by 1 August 1938[4]. The Politburo wrote its justification into the resolution itself: "enemies of the people - Trotskyites, Bukharinites and bourgeois nationalists operating in the People's Commissariat of Education of the Ukrainian SSR - implanted special national German, Polish, Czech, Swedish, Greek and other schools, turning them into hotbeds of bourgeois-nationalist, anti-Soviet influence on children"[4]. The decision was given the form of a state act by the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR in its resolution of 29 June 1938 on the reorganization of special national schools, colleges and the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute: by 1 August 1938, 766 national primary, incomplete secondary and secondary schools were subject to reorganization into ordinary schools with (predominantly) Russian and Ukrainian as the language of instruction, and another 122 were merged with Russian and Ukrainian ones on the territorial principle - the count of the historian Liudmyla Yakubova[11]. |

</details>

posts.title: Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) (C0081)

The collusion of two totalitarian regimes (the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact), which led to the USSR's invasion of Poland and the seizure of Western Ukraine. To legitimize the occupation, the "People's Assembly of Western Ukraine 1939" was staged, which "on October 27 in Lviv… adopted the Declaration on the reunification of Western Ukraine with the Ukrainian SSR"[1]. Then came the mass deportations: "Between September 1939 and June 1941, up to 1,250,000 people (about 10% of the population) were removed from these lands and Western Belarus… to remote regions of the USSR"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (8)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0039 Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0009 Diplomacy (T0039Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The partition of Eastern Europe behind the backs of its peoples: the secret protocol established that "in the event of a territorial-political rearrangement of the areas belonging to the Polish state, the boundary of the spheres of interest of Germany and the USSR shall run approximately along the line of the rivers Narew, Vistula, and San"[3]. Half a century later the Congress of People's Deputies of the USSR "recognizes the secret protocols as legally untenable and invalid from the moment of their signing"[4]. The invasion was covered by Molotov's note to the Polish ambassador Grzybowski (17 September 1939): "the Polish state and its government have in fact ceased to exist"[5]. |
| **[T0019 Military Intervention September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0010 Regular Army (T0019Military Intervention)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The direct armed invasion of Polish territory by the Red Army on September 17, 1939 for the military occupation of the western Ukrainian lands; the seizure was consolidated by "the treaty of the USSR with Germany (September 28, 1939)," which "confirmed the incorporation of the western Ukrainian lands into the USSR"[6]. |
| **[T0109 Sham Expression of Popular Will September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations (T0109Sham Expression of Popular Will)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/369):** The staging of a no-alternative "People's Assembly" under the control of occupation troops to give the seizure legal form: "On October 27 in Lviv, the People's Assembly of Western Ukraine of 1939 adopted the Declaration on the reunification of Western Ukraine with the Ukrainian SSR, and on November 1 the Supreme Soviet of the USSR passed the law admitting Western Ukraine, as part of the Ukrainian SSR, into the USSR"[1]. |
| **[T0017 Annexation of Territories September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0017Annexation of Territories)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/325):** The official annexation of the occupied lands: the western Ukrainian lands were incorporated into the USSR under the treaty with Germany of September 28, 1939[6], and "after the Red Army occupied Bessarabia and Northern Bukovyna at the end of June 1940, on August 2, 1940 the Supreme Soviet of the USSR annexed Northern Bukovyna and the Khotyn, Akkerman, and Izmail districts of Bessarabia to the Ukrainian SSR"[1]. |
| **[T0127 Deportation September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0127Deportation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/399):** Mass forced resettlement by quota: "under the resolutions of the Council of People's Commissars of December 5, 1939 and March 2, 1940, subject to administrative resettlement were the employees of the former state institutions, courts, police, army, merchants, Polish settlers, landowners, owners of plants and factories, and their families"; in total "up to 1,250,000 people were removed to remote regions of the USSR"[2]. The waves were separate: the osadniks were deported under the USSR Sovnarkom resolution of December 5, 1939, no. 2010-558ss - its text remains in the closed Archive of the President of the Russian Federation (fond 93), while the mechanics of the operation are known from the NKVD Instruction approved on December 29, 1939[7]; the families of officers, policemen and prison guards were deported under the resolution of March 2, 1940, no. 289-127ss[8]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The neutralization of the politically active stratum through mass arrests: immediately after the "People's Assembly" came "the arrests of leading figures of the Ukrainian intelligentsia, by lists prepared in advance, drawn up in the Soviet consulate"[9]; "in all, in 1939—1941 the NKVD organs arrested 21,982 Poles, 23,163 Ukrainians and 13,160 Jews"[9], and those arrested faced execution, prison or the GULAG camps: "in total, during 1939—1941, between 16 and 35 thousand OUN members were shot or imprisoned"[9]. |
| **[T0057 Labor Exploitation September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0057Labor Exploitation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The transfer of hundreds of thousands of people into special settlements and camps as a system of forced labor: in under two years "up to 1,250,000 people were removed to remote regions of the USSR"[2] – the deportees were assigned to labor in remote regions with no right to leave. |
| **[T0158 Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0158Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** The sign of the new order goes up within the very first weeks: Soviet troops took Lviv on 22 September 1939[10], and already in October, in the city center, on the islet in the middle of today's Svobody Avenue, rose the monument to the Stalin Constitution - a huge vertical composition of columns entwined with red banners, on a wooden frame, with five sculptural groups (a Red Army soldier, a worker, a mother with a child, a female student, and an old Hutsul with a boy) and inscriptions in Ukrainian, Polish and Yiddish symbolizing the "friendship of peoples" according to the articles of the Stalin constitution[11][12]. The sign has named authors: the sculptor Serhii Lytvynenko and the Kyiv artist Mykhailo Dmytrenko, who arrived in Lviv in 1939 in the "landing party" of Soviet artists whose task was the implantation of socialist realism; possibly the authors merely adapted to the site a design produced in Moscow, and it was executed by the sculptors Yevhen Dzyndra and Andrii Koverko[11]. The monument stood until 30 June 1941 and vanished with the arrival of the Germans[11]. |

</details>

posts.title: Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945) (C0082)

The Soviet authorities' treatment of Ukraine as a colonial resource during the war. During the 1941 retreat the directive of the USSR Sovnarkom and the Central Committee of 29 June 1941 was in force: "In the forced withdrawal of Red Army units… leave the enemy not a kilogram of grain, not a liter of fuel… All valuable property… that cannot be evacuated must without fail be destroyed"[1]. In 1943–1944, on the liberated territory, the mobilization of the "chornosvytnyky" was carried out: they were "thrown into combat often at once, without undergoing military training… sometimes unarmed, not even changed into military uniform"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0105 Total Destruction of Infrastructure June 1941 C0082 Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945) G0010 USSR S0010 Regular Army (T0105Total Destruction of Infrastructure)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/366):** The 1941 scorched-earth tactic under the directive of the USSR Sovnarkom and the Central Committee of 29 June 1941: "In the forced withdrawal of Red Army units, drive off the rolling railway stock, leave the enemy not a single locomotive, not a single railcar"[1]; the Dnipro hydroelectric station was "destroyed at the beginning of the Great Patriotic War… (see the Directive of the USSR Council of People's Commissars and the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of June 29, 1941)"[3]. |
| **[T0052 Expropriation of Resources June 1941 C0082 Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945) G0010 USSR S0008 Government (T0052Expropriation of Resources)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** The total removal of industrial equipment and food supplies into the interior of the USSR: "550 industrial facilities were moved into the interior of the USSR (190 of all-Union and 360 of republican subordination)"; "From the Right Bank to the left bank of the Dnipro were ferried 4,498 tractors, 680 combines, 690 motor vehicles"[4]. |
| **[T0049 Forced Mobilization June 1941 C0082 Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945) G0010 USSR S0010 Regular Army (T0049Forced Mobilization)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The mass conscription by field draft offices of the population of just-liberated territories: "'Chornosvytnyky' or 'black infantry' – such was the unofficial name given to men and youths mobilized by field military commissariats, and in fact by the commanders of formations, units, and detachments in 1943–1944 after the Red Army's liberation of enemy-occupied territories"[2]. |
| **[T0134 Use as Cannon Fodder June 1941 C0082 Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945) G0010 USSR S0010 Regular Army (T0134Use as Cannon Fodder)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/406):** The use of untrained conscripts as expendable material: they were "thrown into combat often at once, without undergoing military training in reserve units, sometimes unarmed, not even changed into military uniform (hence the name)"[2]. The scale is visible from a single episode: "after the Red Army first took Kharkiv in the spring of 1943, about 15 thousand people aged 15 to 45 were mobilized into it and sent to the front without training," with "1 rifle per 5-10 men"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) (C0084)

A war waged by NKVD/MGB troops against the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) in western Ukraine: chekist-military operations, mass repressive actions, and the forced removal of insurgents' families to Siberia - in 1944–52 "203,662 people were deported from the territory of Western Ukraine to special settlements in remote regions of the USSR"[1]. Its finale was the use of collusion with a third party - Operation "Vistula" (1947), coordinated with the pro-Soviet government of Poland, "the concluding stage of the forced deportation of Ukrainians" "from the ancestral lands of Lemkivshchyna, Nadsiannia, Kholmshchyna, and Pidliashshia," carried out to deprive the UPA of its social base[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0077 Punitive Expeditions January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0077Punitive Expeditions)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/359):** Regular chekist-military operations by the NKVD and MGB to sweep western Ukrainian villages: the People's Commissar of Internal Affairs of the Ukrainian SSR T. Strokach personally "directed and coordinated operational-chekist operations to liquidate the underground of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists and units of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, and mass deportations of the population in Western Ukraine"[3]. Already "on April 5, 1944, on the basis of a directive of the People's Commissariat of Internal Affairs of the USSR, a scheme of arrests and deportation of OUN–UPA members was worked out"[1]. |
| **[T0104 Mass Killings of Civilians January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0104Mass Killings of Civilians)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** Extrajudicial killings of civilians in the course of suppressing the insurgency: the Presidium of the CPSU Central Committee itself admitted, in its resolution "On the Political and Economic Situation of the Western Oblasts of the Ukrainian SSR" of May 26, 1953: "From 1944 through 1952, up to 500 thousand people in the western oblasts of Ukraine were subjected to various kinds of repression, including over 134 thousand arrested, over 153 thousand killed, and over 203 thousand deported forever from the Ukrainian SSR"[4][5] – the authorities did not divide the killed into insurgents and civilians, and already on July 2, 1953, after Beria's arrest, the resolution itself was revoked as conducive to "the activization of bourgeois-nationalist elements"[4]. Terror was also waged by disguised MGB "special groups" acting under the guise of the UPA: the military prosecutor of the MVD troops of the Ukrainian district, Kosharsky, in his report to Khrushchev (February 15, 1949), cited "examples of beatings, rapes and robberies of the population" by agent-fighters and stated: "the actions of the so-called MGB special groups are of a pronounced bandit, anti-Soviet character and, of course, cannot be justified by any operational considerations"[6]. |
| **[T0022 Terror January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0022Terror)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** The creation of an atmosphere of total fear through the bloody provocations of NKVD special groups operating in the guise of the UPA: People's Commissar Strokach "initiated the formation of special groups of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR from former partisans for the struggle against the UPA" and "personally interrogated the captured leaders of the OUN networks of Western Ukraine"[3]. The terror was also demonstrative: "one of the forms of struggle was the policy of intimidating OUN and UPA members and the local population: open trials and executions, putting the bodies of the dead on public display, and destroying insurgent graves"[7]. |
| **[T0039 Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0009 Diplomacy (T0039Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The coordination of actions with the pro-Soviet government of Poland to destroy the Ukrainian underground: Operation "Vistula," "as a deportation action, was elaborated in detail and carried out by the Polish authorities," but its execution "was coordinated with the party-Soviet organs of power of the USSR" - the Soviet command transferred "from Lviv oblast one tank division and special NKVD units, and blocked the Ukrainian-Polish border with border troops"[2]. |
| **[T0127 Deportation January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0127Deportation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/399):** The forcible removal of insurgents' families to Siberia and the deportation of the Ukrainians of Zakerzonnia: the removal of "bandit accomplices" with their entire families began at once - already in the summer of 1944 "more than 17,000 people were carried off to Krasnoyarsk Krai"[1]; in all, in 1944–52, 203,662 people were removed to special settlements, among them "representatives of the families of members of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists and soldiers of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army and their sympathizers — 182,543 people"[1]. Operation "Vistula" was carried out in order to "deprive it of socio-economic and moral-psychological support from the local Ukrainian population," and ended in the scattering of the community: the authorities rid themselves of the Ukrainian population, "dispersing about 150 thousand people"[2]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Mass arrests of UPA fighters, OUN members, and those suspected of aiding them, followed by dispatch to the GULAG camps, upon which the regime placed "the isolation of 'unreliable elements'" as one of its key tasks[5]. During Operation "Vistula," for civilians suspected of assisting the underground there was provision for "the introduction of courts-martial and concentration camps, in particular at Jaworzno"[2]. By 1951 Ukrainians had become the second-largest nation of the GULAG: according to the agency's own statistics, the "National composition of GULAG prisoners (as of January 1, 1951)" counted 506,221 Ukrainians out of some 2.5 million prisoners - about 20%[8]. |
| **[T0057 Labor Exploitation January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0057Labor Exploitation)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The use of captured resistance members and deportees as free labor: the tasks of the GULAG included "using them as cheap labor and transferring them, as needed, from place to place"[5]; deportees from Western Ukraine were sent to special settlements and hard labor - in the summer of 1944 alone "more than 17,000 people were carried off to Krasnoyarsk Krai"[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: Postwar Ideological Terror ("Zhdanovshchina") (1946–1953)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Postwar Ideological Terror ("Zhdanovshchina") (1946–1953) (C0085)

A return to total control over culture after the relative relaxations of the war years: the rout of the Ukrainian creative intelligentsia, accusations of "bourgeois nationalism" (attacks on Rylsky, Yanovsky, the persecution of Sosiura for the poem "Love Ukraine"). In parallel ran a state antisemitic campaign: "On July 18, 1952 the Military Collegium of the USSR Supreme Court passed death sentences on 13 people, including 5 natives of Ukraine… on August 12, 1952 they were all executed"[1], and in January 1953 the "Doctors' Plot" began.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[T0101 Censorship August 1946 C0085 Postwar Ideological Terror ("Zhdanovshchina") (1946–1953) G0010 USSR S0021 Propaganda (T0101Censorship)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** Total ideological control over art and the press, the banning of works and the vilification of writers for alleged "bourgeois nationalism." The campaign culminated in the verdict in the case of the Jewish Anti-Fascist Committee: "on July 18, 1952 the Military Collegium of the USSR Supreme Court passed death sentences on 13 people, including 5 natives of Ukraine, well-known Jewish writers and poets"[1]. |
| **[T0022 Terror August 1946 C0085 Postwar Ideological Terror ("Zhdanovshchina") (1946–1953) G0010 USSR S0021 Propaganda (T0022Terror)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** The staging of public political persecution (attacks on Rylsky, Sosiura, Yanovsky, the campaign against "cosmopolitans"), instilling an atmosphere of fear. Its outcome was the execution of the defendants in the JAC case: "on August 12, 1952 they were all executed"[1]. |
| **[T0021 Neutralization of the Opposition August 1946 C0085 Postwar Ideological Terror ("Zhdanovshchina") (1946–1953) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services (T0021Neutralization of the Opposition)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Fabricated repressions against figures of the Ukrainian and Jewish intelligentsia: in the case of the Jewish Anti-Fascist Committee, "on July 18, 1952 the Military Collegium of the USSR Supreme Court passed death sentences on 13 people, including 5 natives of Ukraine, the well-known Jewish writers and poets D. Bergelson, D. Hofshtein, L. Kvitko, P. Markish, I. Fefer. On August 12, 1952 they were all executed"[1]. |

</details>
